flight.description: This field identifies the flight that helps this mission.

role.description: This field gives the role of the flight that helps this mission, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.airborne_control: This value identifies an aircraft, such as an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft, that gives surveillance and control to the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.controller: This value identifies a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)) that gives terminal attack control to the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.escort: This value identifies an escort that defends the mission against enemy aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a support role that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.recovery: This value identifies a personnel recovery flight that collects the aircrew of the mission when they become isolated.
x-enum-descriptions.suppression: This value identifies a flight that neutralizes or degrades the enemy air defences that are a threat to the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.tanker: This value identifies a tanker that gives fuel to the aircraft of the mission in flight.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the flight helps this mission.

Survivor.description: A survivor is an isolated person for this recovery.

authentication_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the authentication of the survivor.

callsign.description: This field gives the call sign of the survivor, as free text.

condition.description: This field gives the medical condition of the survivor, as one of the enumerated values.

id.description: This field identifies this survivor. Each survivor in its brief has a different identifier.

isoprep_ref.description: This field gives the identifier of the isolated personnel report (ISOPREP) of the survivor, as free text. The brief contains only this identifier and no other data about the person.

last_known.description: This field gives the last known position of the survivor and the time of the report.

TACAN.description: A Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) is the channel, band and identifier of a TACAN station.

TargetListEntry.description: A target list entry is an entry on a joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL) or on a time-sensitive target (TST) list.

document.description: This field identifies the joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL) or time-sensitive target (TST) document that contains the entry.

entry.description: This field gives the target number or time-sensitive target (TST) number of the entry, as free text.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the training.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the training occurs.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this training task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

debrief_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flights follow to examine the training after it stops.

events.description: This list contains the events of the training, in order. The events occur in their sequence.

exercise_window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the training occurs.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a training tasking.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the training is for, as free text.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the training sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the limits and conditions that are applicable to this training.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the training, as free text.

TrainingBrief.description: A training brief is the data that aircrews get before a training task.

knock_it_off_channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that is for safety calls.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the lowest altitude for the training, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

range_controller.description: This field gives the agency that controls the training range, with its radio channels.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

safety_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the safety instructions of the training.

training_areas.description: This list identifies the training areas, zones and airspace that are for the training.

TransferPoint.description: A load point is an airfield where the load goes into or out of the aircraft, with the time and the procedure.

agency.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that controls the operations with the load.

place.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that receives or sends the load.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the steps for the load.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the load goes into or out of the aircraft.

abort_criteria.description: This list contains the conditions in which the flights stop the transport mission.

brief.description: This field gives the data of the mission brief for this transport task. The brief refers to the records of the resource catalogue and does not copy them.

delivery_method.description: This field gives the method that moves the load out of the aircraft at the airfield that receives it, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.airdrop: The aircraft releases the load in flight.
x-enum-descriptions.hover: The load goes out of the aircraft while the aircraft stays at one position in the air.
x-enum-descriptions.land: The aircraft lands, and then the load goes out of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.sling_load: The load is a sling load below the aircraft until the aircraft releases it.

delivery_time.description: This field gives the time condition for the load at the airfield that receives it. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

destination.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that receives the load.

ground_coordination.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that coordinates the transport on the ground.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a transport tasking.

loading_procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that the flight follows to put the cargo and the persons on the aircraft.

manifest.description: This field gives the cargo and the persons on the aircraft of the transport mission.

objective.description: This field gives the result that the transport mission is for, as free text.

pickup.description: This field identifies the airfield, carrier or forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) that the flight collects the load from.

pickup_time.description: This field gives the time condition for the collection of the load. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

report_refs.description: This list identifies the report definitions of the reports that the transport mission sends. Each identifier refers to the `reports` map of the resource catalogue.

role.description: This field gives the function of the transport mission, as one of the enumerated values. The field `delivery_method` gives how the load goes out of the aircraft.

x-enum-descriptions.aeromedical_evacuation: This value identifies the movement of patients by air. Medical personnel control the patients and give them treatment en-route.
x-enum-descriptions.air_assault: This value identifies an air assault. The aircraft are helicopters or tiltrotor aircraft. They move assault forces that engage enemy forces or hold terrain.
x-enum-descriptions.airdrop: This value identifies an airdrop of personnel or materiel from aircraft in flight.
x-enum-descriptions.airlift: This value identifies the movement of personnel and materiel by air.
x-enum-descriptions.humanitarian_assistance: This value identifies airlift for a humanitarian assistance operation.
x-enum-descriptions.noncombatant_evacuation: This value identifies airlift for a noncombatant evacuation operation.

success_criteria.description: This field gives the conditions that show a satisfactory result of the transport mission, as free text.

TransportBrief.description: A transport brief is the data for a transport mission.

air_assault.description: This field gives the air assault data. A transport task with the `air_assault` role shall have this field.

airdrop.description: This field gives the airdrop data. A transport task with the `airdrop` role shall have this field.

load_plan.description: This list contains the loads of the flights.

flight.description: This field identifies the flight that has this load.

manifest.description: This field gives the cargo and the passengers of this load.

offload.description: This field gives the airfield, the time and the procedure at which the load goes out of the aircraft.

onload.description: This field gives the airfield, the time and the procedure at which the load goes into the aircraft.

patients.description: This field gives the numbers of patients and attendants for the `aeromedical_evacuation` role.

ambulatory.description: This field gives the number of patients that can walk.

attendants.description: This field gives the number of medical attendants.

litter.description: This field gives the number of patients on litters.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

WeaponLoad.description: A weapon load is the weapons of one flight for an attack assignment, with their fuze settings and altitudes.

attack_heading.description: This field gives the attack heading of the flight, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

flight.description: This field identifies the flight that releases the weapons.

fuze.description: This field gives the fuze setting of the weapons for this attack. If the weapon load does not give it, the fuze of the store in the standard conventional load (SCL) of the flight is applicable.

laser_code.description: This field gives the laser code of the weapons for this attack. If the weapon load does not give it, the laser code of the standard conventional load (SCL) of the flight is applicable.

quantity.description: This field gives the number of weapons for the flight. The quantity shall not be more than all aircraft of the flight have in their standard conventional load (SCL).

release_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude at which the flight releases the weapons, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

scl.description: This field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that contains the weapons. It shall be an SCL of the flight.

store.description: This field identifies the store that is the weapon. When the flight has a standard conventional load (SCL), an SCL of the flight shall contain the store.

Window.description: A window is a time interval with limits that are absolute date-times or offsets from the period of the order that contains it.

airfield.description: An airfield is an aircraft operating location: a fixed airfield with runways, an aircraft carrier or a forward arming and refuelling point (FARP). The record has the position, the radio frequencies, the traffic pattern and the links to navigation records.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

approach_instructions.description: This list contains the local arrival and approach instructions for mission aircraft, as free text.

atis.description: This field gives the static data of the automatic terminal information service (ATIS) broadcast for a simulator. The ATIS frequency is an item of `frequencies` with the role `atis`. The simulator gives the weather.

calm_wind_runway.description: This field gives the designator of the calm wind runway: the runway end that the airfield uses for a calm wind. The value shall be the designator of an end of a runway of this airfield.

carrier.description: This field gives the data of an aircraft carrier. The data are the hull number, the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN), the instrument carrier landing system (ICLS) channel and the case recovery data. A record with a different `kind` shall not have this field.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the air traffic at the airfield.

elevation.description: This field gives the published elevation of the airfield above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

frequencies.description: This list contains the radio frequencies of the stations at the operating location. Each item has the role of the station, for example tower, ground or automatic terminal information service (ATIS).

hung_ordnance_runway.description: This field gives the designator of the runway end that aircraft with hung ordnance use for landing. A base publishes it in its local emergency procedures. The value shall be the designator of an end of a runway of this airfield. A `carrier` record shall not have this field.

id.description: This field identifies this airfield. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this airfield.

ident.description: This field identifies this airfield in published data. Examples are the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) location indicator and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) identifier.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the operating location, as one of the enumerated values. An `airfield` record shall have `position`, `elevation` and one or more runways. A `farp` record shall have `position` and `elevation`, and no runways. A `carrier` record shall have `carrier`, and no runways or landing pads.

x-enum-descriptions.airfield: This value identifies a fixed airfield with one or more runways.
x-enum-descriptions.carrier: This value identifies an aircraft carrier. Its position comes from its unit in the simulator.
x-enum-descriptions.farp: This value identifies a forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) with landing pads.

localizers.description: This list identifies the localizers that are for the runways of this airfield. When a localizer in this list identifies an airfield, that airfield shall be this airfield.

magnetic_variation_deg.description: This field gives the magnetic variation at the airfield, in degrees. Values for east are more than zero, and values for west are less than zero.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airfield, for display.

navaids.description: This list contains the navigation aids of the airfield: `VOR`, `VORTAC`, `TACAN`, `NDB` or `DME` stations. The Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of a fixed airfield or a forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) is in this list. It is a `TACAN` or `VORTAC` station. When a navigation aid in this list identifies an airfield, that airfield shall be this airfield.

operating_hours.description: This field gives the hours of each week, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), when the operating location is open. The schedule is the same for all weeks, and the location is not open at other times. When the record does not have this field, the location is always open.

pads.description: This list contains the landing pads of a forward arming and refuelling point (FARP) or of a helicopter area of an airfield.

parking.description: This list contains the parking stands of the operating location.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the airfield reference point, as latitude and longitude.

procedures.description: This list identifies the instrument procedures that start or stop at this airfield: standard instrument departure (SID), standard terminal arrival route (STAR) or approach. When a procedure in this list identifies an airfield, that airfield shall be this airfield.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this airfield as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airfield. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

runways.description: This list contains the runways of the airfield. Each item is one runway with its two ends.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

taxi.description: This field gives the taxi graph of the airfield: the taxi nodes, with their names, and the edges between them. The graph does not give the shape of the taxiways.

traffic_pattern.description: This field gives the traffic pattern of the airfield. Its values are the default values. A runway end can give different values for that end.

transition_altitude.description: This field gives the transition altitude, as an altitude with its unit and reference. At or below this altitude, the vertical position of an aircraft is its altitude above mean sea level.

use.description: This field gives the use of the operating location: civil, military, or joint civil and military use, as one of the enumerated values. Aerodrome data publish it.

x-enum-descriptions.civil: This value identifies an operating location for civil aviation.
x-enum-descriptions.joint: This value identifies an operating location that civil aviation and armed forces use together.
x-enum-descriptions.military: This value identifies an operating location of armed forces.

airfield.title: Airfield

airfield.Atis.description: Automatic terminal information service (ATIS) data is the static data that a simulator puts into the ATIS broadcast. The weather is not part of this data.

remarks.description: This list contains the notes at the end of the broadcast, as free text.

runway_in_use.description: This field gives the designator of the active runway end in the broadcast. The value shall be the designator of an end of a runway of this airfield.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the transition level: flight level (`FL`).

transition_level.description: This field gives the transition level that the broadcast gives, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

airfield.Carrier.description: An aircraft carrier is a record with the identifier and the recovery data of an aircraft carrier. The carrier moves, and thus its position comes from its unit in the simulator.

acls.description: The value is `true` when the carrier has an automatic carrier landing system (ACLS) for the recovery of aircraft. The value is `false` when the carrier has no ACLS.

case_recovery.description: This field gives the case recovery that the carrier plans, and the marshal data.

hull_number.description: This field identifies this carrier as its hull number. An example is `CVN-72`.

icls_channel.description: This field gives the channel of the instrument carrier landing system (ICLS) of the carrier, from 1 to 20.

link4.description: This field gives the frequency of the Link 4 data link of the carrier, in megahertz.

recovery_windows.description: This list contains the recovery windows of the carrier, in order.

tacan.description: This field gives the channel and the band of the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of the carrier. The TACAN moves with the ship, and thus it is not a fixed navigation aid in `navaids`.

airfield.CaseRecovery.description: A case recovery is the recovery procedure that a carrier plans, and the position of its marshal stack. The marshal frequency is an item of `frequencies` with the role `marshal`.

case.description: This field gives the case recovery that the carrier plans, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.case_i: This value identifies the Case `I` recovery for visual conditions by day.
x-enum-descriptions.case_ii: This value identifies the Case `II` recovery: a descent in instrument conditions to visual conditions below the cloud.
x-enum-descriptions.case_iii: This value identifies the Case `III` recovery for instrument conditions, or for a recovery at night.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the marshal altitude: mean sea level (`MSL`).

marshal_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the lowest level of the marshal stack, above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

marshal_distance.description: This field gives the distance of the marshal stack from the carrier, as a length with its unit.

marshal_radial.description: This field gives the radial from the carrier on which the marshal stack is, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

airfield.GoAround.description: A go-around is the local climb-out instructions for a go-around. When the record has no heading, aircraft fly the runway heading.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the go-around altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude to which aircraft climb on a go-around, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

heading.description: This field gives the heading that aircraft fly on a go-around, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

airfield.InitialPoint.description: An initial point is the start of the initial leg of an overhead pattern. It is a point with a name, or a distance and a bearing from the runway threshold.

point.description: This field gives the point, with its name, at the start of the initial leg.

bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the runway threshold to the initial point, as a bearing with its unit and reference. When the record does not have this field, the point is on the extended centreline of the runway.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from the runway threshold to the initial point, as a length with its unit.

airfield.Pad.description: A pad is one prepared surface of the operating location: a helicopter or vertical landing pad, or a ground pad for aircraft with live ordnance or hot brakes. A pad without a use is a landing pad.

name.description: This field gives the name of this pad, for display.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the pad, as latitude and longitude.

use.description: This list contains the uses of the ground pad. One pad can have more than one use.

x-enum-descriptions.arm_dearm: This value identifies an arming and disarming area at the end of the runway, where ground crews arm aircraft before take-off and disarm them after landing.
x-enum-descriptions.hot_brake: This value identifies a hot brake area, where aircraft with hot brakes stop until the brakes are cool.
x-enum-descriptions.hung_ordnance: This value identifies a hung ordnance area, where ground crews make safe the ordnance that did not release.

airfield.PatternSet.description: Pattern values are the values of a traffic pattern for one aircraft category. Each value is optional.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the pattern altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the rectangular traffic pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

break_point.description: This field gives the position along the runway at which aircraft start the overhead break, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.approach_end: The overhead break starts above the approach end of the runway.
x-enum-descriptions.departure_end: The overhead break starts above the departure end of the runway.
x-enum-descriptions.midfield: The overhead break starts above the middle of the runway.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the departure ceiling: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

departure_ceiling.description: This field gives the highest altitude for departures while aircraft use the overhead pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

direction.description: This field gives the direction of the turns in the traffic pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.left: Each turn in the pattern is a left turn.
x-enum-descriptions.right: Each turn in the pattern is a right turn.

go_around.description: This field gives the go-around instructions of the pattern.

initial.description: This list contains the initial points of the overhead pattern.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the overhead altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

overhead_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the initial leg and of the overhead break, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

reentry.description: This field gives the re-entry procedure of the overhead pattern.

sfo.description: This field gives the simulated flameout (SFO) pattern. When the record has no SFO pattern, the pattern values do not give one.

airfield.RecoveryWindow.description: A recovery window is a time interval in which the carrier recovers aircraft with one case recovery.

brc.description: This field gives the base recovery course, which is the heading of the carrier during the recovery, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

case.description: This field gives the case recovery in the window, as one of the enumerated values.

window.description: This field gives the time interval during which the carrier recovers aircraft.

airfield.Reentry.description: A re-entry is the procedure that aircraft use to enter the overhead pattern again. It has the point or the name of the re-entry point, and its altitude.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the re-entry altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the re-entry, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

name.description: This field gives the name of the re-entry point, when no point record identifies it, as free text.

point.description: This field identifies the point at which aircraft start the re-entry.

airfield.SimulatedFlameout.description: A simulated flameout pattern is the altitudes of the high key and the low key of a simulated flameout (SFO) pattern. The base publishes them.

high_key.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the high key, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. The block gives the altitudes that aircraft can use at the high key.

low_key.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the low key, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. The block gives the altitudes that aircraft can use at the low key.

airfield.Stand.description: A parking stand is one parking position for one aircraft.

category.description: This field gives the largest aircraft class that can use the parking stand, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.fighter: This value identifies fighters and other small aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.heavy: This value identifies heavy aircraft, for example a tanker aircraft or a large transport aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.helicopter: This value identifies a stand or a taxiway only for helicopters, not for fixed-wing aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.medium: This value identifies aircraft of moderate dimensions, for example a transport aircraft with two engines.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

heading.description: This field gives the heading of an aircraft on the parking stand, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

helicopters.description: The value is `true` when helicopters can also use the parking stand.

id.description: This field identifies this parking stand. Each parking stand in its airfield has a different identifier. A taxi node refers to the parking stand with this identifier.

length.description: This field gives the length of the parking stand, as a length with its unit.

name.description: This field gives the name of the parking stand in the radio calls of air traffic control (ATC), for example `41`, as free text.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the parking stand, as latitude and longitude.

ramp.description: This field gives the name of the ramp or apron of the parking stand, as free text.

shelter.description: The value is `true` when the parking stand is in an aircraft shelter.

width.description: This field gives the width of the parking stand, as a length with its unit.

airfield.StationFrequency.description: A station frequency is one radio frequency of a station at an operating location, with the role of the station.

callsign.description: This field gives the radio callsign of the station, for example `Muwaffaq Salti Tower`, as free text.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the station frequency: megahertz (`MHz`).

frequency.description: This field gives the frequency of the station, as a frequency with its unit. The unit is megahertz, and the field `modulation` is mandatory.

hours.description: This field gives the hours of each week, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), when the station uses this frequency. When the record does not have this field, the station uses the frequency during the hours of the operating location.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this frequency, as free text.

role.description: This field gives the role of the station on this frequency, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.approach: This value identifies the approach control. On a military airfield, it is the radar approach control (RAPCON).
x-enum-descriptions.atis: This value identifies the automatic terminal information service (ATIS) broadcast, which gives the weather, the active runway and other airfield information all the time.
x-enum-descriptions.clearance_delivery: This value identifies the clearance delivery for instrument flight rules (IFR) clearances before taxi.
x-enum-descriptions.departure: This value identifies the departure control. It controls instrument flight rules (IFR) flights after they take off, until the en-route centre controls them.
x-enum-descriptions.final: This value identifies the final controller of a precision approach radar (PAR) approach. The final controller gives the azimuth and glide path corrections.
x-enum-descriptions.ground: This value identifies the ground control for the movement area.
x-enum-descriptions.marshal: This value identifies the carrier marshal control for recovery.
x-enum-descriptions.ops: This value identifies the operations desk of the unit or of the forward arming and refuelling point (FARP).
x-enum-descriptions.pmsv: This value identifies the pilot-to-metro service (PMSV) for weather information.
x-enum-descriptions.tower: This value identifies the aerodrome control tower. On a carrier, it is the primary flight control.
x-enum-descriptions.unicom: This value identifies the universal communications (UNICOM) at an airfield without a control tower.

airfield.TaxiEdge.description: A taxi edge is a taxi route between two taxi nodes.

category.description: This field gives the largest aircraft class that can use the edge, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.fighter: This value identifies fighters and other small aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.heavy: This value identifies heavy aircraft, for example a tanker aircraft or a large transport aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.helicopter: This value identifies a stand or a taxiway only for helicopters, not for fixed-wing aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.medium: This value identifies aircraft of moderate dimensions, for example a transport aircraft with two engines.

from.description: This field identifies the taxi node that is at the start of the edge. The value shall be the identifier of a node of this graph.

one_way.description: The value is `true` when aircraft can taxi on the edge only from `from` to `to`. The value is `false` when aircraft can taxi on the edge in the two directions.

taxiway.description: This field gives the name of the taxiway of the edge, for example `Alpha`, as free text.

to.description: This field identifies the taxi node that is at the end of the edge. The value shall be the identifier of a different node of this graph.

width.description: This field gives the width of the taxiway of the edge, as a length with its unit.

airfield.TaxiGraph.description: A taxi graph is the taxi routes of an airfield as nodes and edges. A program finds a taxi route along the edges from a parking stand to a hold-short node.

edges.description: This list contains the edges between the taxi nodes.

nodes.description: This list contains the taxi nodes of the airfield.

airfield.TaxiNode.description: A taxi node is one point of the taxi graph.

id.description: This field identifies this taxi node. Each taxi node in its airfield has a different identifier.

kind.description: This field gives the type of the taxi node, as one of the enumerated values. A `hold_short` or `runway_connection` node shall have `runway_end`. A `parking` node shall have `stand`.

x-enum-descriptions.hold_short: This value identifies a hold-short point before a runway. Aircraft stop at this point until they get a clearance.
x-enum-descriptions.intersection: This value identifies a point where two or more taxiways connect.
x-enum-descriptions.parking: This value identifies a point where the taxi graph connects to a parking stand.
x-enum-descriptions.runway: This value identifies a point on the runway centreline.
x-enum-descriptions.runway_connection: This value identifies a point where a taxiway connects to a runway. Aircraft go onto the runway or off the runway at this point.

name.description: This field gives the name of the taxi node, for example `A3`, as free text.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the taxi node, as latitude and longitude.

runway_end.description: This field gives the designator of the runway end to which this node connects, or before which aircraft stop at this node. The value shall be the designator of an end of a runway of this airfield.

stand.description: This field identifies the parking stand that this node connects to. The value shall be the identifier of a stand of this airfield.

airfield.TrafficPattern.description: A traffic pattern is a set of pattern values, with more values for each aircraft category. A consumer gets each value from the runway end first, then from the airfield, and then from the traffic pattern profile. A value for an aircraft category replaces the general value for that aircraft category.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the pattern altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the rectangular traffic pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

break_point.description: This field gives the position along the runway at which aircraft start the overhead break, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.approach_end: The overhead break starts above the approach end of the runway.
x-enum-descriptions.departure_end: The overhead break starts above the departure end of the runway.
x-enum-descriptions.midfield: The overhead break starts above the middle of the runway.

categories.description: This field gives the pattern values for each aircraft category. Each aircraft category gives only the values that are different.

fighter.description: This field gives the pattern values for fighters and attack aircraft.

heavy.description: This field gives the pattern values for heavy aircraft and tanker aircraft.

helicopter.description: This field gives the pattern values for helicopters.

trainer.description: This field gives the pattern values for trainer aircraft.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the departure ceiling: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

departure_ceiling.description: This field gives the highest altitude for departures while aircraft use the overhead pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

direction.description: This field gives the direction of the turns in the traffic pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.left: Each turn in the pattern is a left turn.
x-enum-descriptions.right: Each turn in the pattern is a right turn.

go_around.description: This field gives the go-around instructions of the pattern.

initial.description: This list contains the initial points of the overhead pattern.

reference.description: This field gives the reference of the overhead altitude: above ground level (`AGL`) or mean sea level (`MSL`).

overhead_altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the initial leg and of the overhead break, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.

profile.description: This field identifies the traffic pattern profile that gives the values that this pattern does not give.

reentry.description: This field gives the re-entry procedure of the overhead pattern.

sfo.description: This field gives the simulated flameout (SFO) pattern. When the record has no SFO pattern, the pattern values do not give one.

airspace.description: Airspace is a region of airspace with a name, made of volumes that each have a horizontal boundary and vertical limits. The `airspace_type` field gives the class or the type of operation. Shelves, sectors and subtracted volumes use the same structure of components. The control measures for air traffic in Annex B use this contract. Examples are class B airspace, control zones and restricted areas.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

airspace_class_code.description: This field gives the airspace class that the source gives, as one of the enumerated values. When the code is empty, the source gives no class. All classes use the same structure for geometry and altitude.

airspace_type.description: This field gives the class or type of operation of the airspace, such as `ClassB`, `ClassD`, `MTA` or `TMA`, as one of the enumerated values. `MTA` is a military training area, and `TMA` is a terminal control area.

x-enum-descriptions.ADIZ: An air defence identification zone (ADIZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the identification, location and control of aircraft is immediately necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ATCAA: An air traffic control assigned airspace (ATCAA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral limits that air traffic control (ATC) assigns. It separates the stated activities in it from other instrument flight rules (IFR) air traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.ATZ: An aerodrome traffic zone (ATZ) is airspace of defined dimensions around an aerodrome. Its function is the protection of aerodrome traffic.
x-enum-descriptions.Alert: An alert area is airspace that can contain a large quantity of pilot training or an unusual type of flight. This training and these flights are not dangerous to aircraft. Charts show the area to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about it. All flights in it obey the Code of Federal Regulations. Each pilot in it has the same task of collision avoidance.
x-enum-descriptions.CFA: A controlled firing area (CFA) is airspace that contains activities that are a danger to non-participating aircraft when they are not in a controlled environment. They stop at once when spotter aircraft, radar or ground observers find an aircraft that approaches.
x-enum-descriptions.CTA: A control area (CTA) is controlled airspace that extends upwards from a given limit above the surface. Its floor is above the surface, not at the surface. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.CTR: A control zone (CTR) is controlled airspace from the surface to a given upper limit. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassA: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class A airspace is airspace only for instrument flight rules (IFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassB: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class B airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other. In the United States, ATC separates VFR flights with radar. When the radar does not operate, ATC stops this service for VFR flights.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassC: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class C airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights from all other flights, and VFR flights from IFR flights. VFR flights get traffic information about other VFR flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassD: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class D airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. IFR flights get traffic information about VFR flights, and VFR flights get traffic information about all other flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassE: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class E airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. Only IFR flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary only for IFR flights. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. All flights get traffic information as far as practical. A control zone cannot be class E airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassF: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class F airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. Participating IFR flights get an air traffic advisory service, which separates them from other IFR flights as far as practical. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it. The United States does not use class F airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.ClassG: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class G airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service or separation, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it.
x-enum-descriptions.Danger: A danger area is airspace of defined dimensions in which tasks that are dangerous to the flight of aircraft can occur at stated times. This definition comes from air traffic control.
x-enum-descriptions.FIR: A flight information region (FIR) is airspace of defined dimensions in which flight information service and alerting service are available.
x-enum-descriptions.MOA: A military operations area (MOA) is airspace that is not in class A airspace. It separates flight training of armed forces that is not dangerous from instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft. It also shows visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft where this training occurs. When it is active, air traffic control (ATC) lets an IFR flight go through it only when ATC can separate the flight.
x-enum-descriptions.MTA: A military training area (MTA) is a geographical area that is temporarily or permanently for education and training, which includes exercises and testing. It can include airspace. AJP-3.3.5 gives this area as the training area (TRNG).
x-enum-descriptions.ModeCVeil: A mode C veil is the airspace that is 30 nautical miles or less from an airport in Appendix D, section 1 of 14 CFR part 91. It goes from the surface to 10,000 feet above mean sea level (MSL). Unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes a different procedure, aircraft in it have a serviceable transponder with automatic altitude reporting and serviceable `ADS-B Out` equipment.
x-enum-descriptions.NSA: A national security area (NSA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral dimensions at locations with ground facilities. At these locations, it is necessary to increase security and safety. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) tells pilots to avoid flight through it. A temporary flight restriction (TFR) can temporarily close it to flight.
x-enum-descriptions.Other: The airspace has a local type that is not in this list. The `local_type` field gives the local name of the type.
x-enum-descriptions.Prohibited: A prohibited area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. The state prohibits flight in it.
x-enum-descriptions.RMZ: A radio mandatory zone (RMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of radio equipment is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.ROZ: A restricted operating zone (ROZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates for a given situation or operational need. Examples are refuelling orbits, holding, fires and landing or drop zones. It restricts the operation of one or more airspace users in it.
x-enum-descriptions.Restricted: A restricted area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. In it, the conditions that the state gives restrict the flight of aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.SFRA: A special flight rules area (SFRA) is airspace of defined dimensions, above land areas or territorial waters. In it, the flight of aircraft obeys 14 CFR part 93, unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions.Sector: A control sector is airspace of known horizontal and vertical dimensions. One controller or a group of controllers controls the air traffic in it. The primary traffic flows, the altitude layers and the work of the controllers set its limits. Pilots in it usually speak to air traffic control (ATC) on the frequencies of the sector.
x-enum-descriptions.TFR: A temporary flight restriction (TFR) is a regulatory action of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a notice to air missions (NOTAM). It temporarily restricts some aircraft from operation in a defined area. Its function is the protection of persons or property in the air or on the ground.
x-enum-descriptions.TMA: A terminal control area (TMA) is a control area, usually at the confluence of air traffic services routes near one or more major aerodromes. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
x-enum-descriptions.TMZ: A transponder mandatory zone (TMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of a pressure-altitude reporting transponder is mandatory.
x-enum-descriptions.TRA: A temporary reserved area (TRA) is a defined volume of airspace that one airspace authority usually controls. By common agreement, it is temporarily for another airspace authority. Other air traffic may transit it only with air traffic control (ATC) clearance.
x-enum-descriptions.TRSA: A terminal radar service area (TRSA) is airspace around a designated airport. In it, air traffic control (ATC) gives radar vectoring, sequencing and separation full time. This service is for all instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft and participating visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft. This service is not mandatory for pilots. It is not an airspace class.
x-enum-descriptions.TSA: A temporary segregated area (TSA) is airspace of defined dimensions for the exclusive use of specified users. Their tasks make this necessary. It is for a set period, and no other traffic uses the airspace.
x-enum-descriptions.UIR: An upper flight information region (UIR) is a flight information region (FIR) above a different FIR. Its floor is the ceiling of the lower FIR and is a visual flight rules (VFR) cruising level. Its procedures can be different from the procedures of the lower FIR.
x-enum-descriptions.Warning: A warning area is airspace of known dimensions that starts 3 nautical miles from the coast of the United States. It contains tasks that can be dangerous to non-participating aircraft. Its function is to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about this risk. It can be above the waters of the United States, above international waters or above the two.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace.

components.description: This list contains the airspace volumes of this airspace, in order. Each volume has a floor and a ceiling.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this airspace and its local conditions, as free text.

designator.description: This field gives the designator that a publication or an assignment gives to the airspace. An example is the designator of a restricted area.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airspace. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace.

local_type.description: This field gives the local type name of the airspace when `airspace_type` is `Other`, as free text.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airspace, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace.

state.description: This field gives the State responsible for the airspace, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code such as `DEU`. Under International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 11, paragraph 2.1, this State is responsible for the air traffic services in the airspace. An example is the State of a flight information region (FIR).

type.description: The value identifies this record as an airspace, which is a region made of airspace volumes.

airspace.title: Airspace

airway.description: An airway is an en-route route as a sequence of fixes, with the course, the distance and the altitude limits of each segment.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

airway_type.description: This field gives the class of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.advisory: This value identifies a designated route along which air traffic advisory service is available.
x-enum-descriptions.air_traffic_services: This value identifies a specified route that channels the flow of traffic, as necessary to supply air traffic services.
x-enum-descriptions.airway: This value identifies a control area, or a part of it, in the shape of a corridor. Radio navigation aids identify the corridor.
x-enum-descriptions.area_navigation: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route for aircraft that can do area navigation.
x-enum-descriptions.conditional: This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route, or a part of it, that is non-permanent. Aircraft plan and use it only under stated conditions.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this airway.

ident.description: This field identifies this airway as published. An example is `V356`.

level.description: This field gives the altitude structure of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.both: This value identifies the low and the high altitude structures.
x-enum-descriptions.high: This value identifies the high altitude structure.
x-enum-descriptions.low: This value identifies the low altitude structure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airway, for display.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this airway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

segments.description: This list contains the fixes, in airway sequence, in order. Each item has a fix and the segment from that fix to the next fix.

items.description: An airway segment is one airway fix and the segment from this fix to the next fix.

directional_restriction.description: This field gives the direction restriction of the segment, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.backward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in the direction opposite to airway sequence.
x-enum-descriptions.forward: Aircraft can fly the segment only in airway sequence.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from this fix to the next fix, as a length with its unit.

fix.description: This field gives the airway fix at the start of this segment.

inbound_course.description: This field gives the course to this fix from the previous fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

maximum_altitude.description: This field gives the maximum authorized altitude (MAA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

minimum_altitude.description: This field gives the minimum en-route altitude (MEA) of the segment from this fix, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

outbound_course.description: This field gives the course from this fix to the next fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure for an airway, with the catalogue code `AIRWAY`. The value selects this contract in a catalogue of control measures.

airway.title: Airway

c2-agency.description: A command and control agency is an organization with a call sign and a role in operations. Units contact it on its radio channels.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

areas.description: This list contains the areas that the agency covers. Each item is a polygon (an openAIX polygon or a GeoJSON polygon), a planning area or a control measure.

callsign.description: This field gives the radio call sign of the agency, as free text.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that other units use to contact the agency.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this agency. Other records and orders use it to refer to this agency.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a command and control agency.

platform.description: This field gives the platform of the agency: on the ground (`ground`) or in an aircraft (`airborne`), as one of the enumerated values.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the agency, as latitude and longitude. The field is applicable only to an agency that does not move.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.

role.description: This field gives the command and control function of the agency, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.AOC: This value identifies the air operations centre (AOC), which plans, controls and assesses air operations. It publishes the air tasking order (ATO) and the airspace control order (ACO).
x-enum-descriptions.ASOC: This value identifies the air support operations centre (ASOC), which controls the air operations that help ground forces directly.
x-enum-descriptions.ATC: This value identifies air traffic control (ATC), which gives air traffic services such as approach control, tower control or range control.
x-enum-descriptions.AWACS: This value identifies the Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS), which gives airborne surveillance, early warning and control.
x-enum-descriptions.CRC: This value identifies the control and reporting centre (CRC), which is an element on the ground for surveillance, identification and control of air operations.
x-enum-descriptions.DASC: This value identifies the direct air support centre (DASC), which is the Marine Corps agency that controls the air operations that help ground forces directly.
x-enum-descriptions.JTAC: This value identifies a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC), who controls close air support (CAS) aircraft from a forward position.
x-enum-descriptions.TACP: This value identifies a tactical air control party (TACP), which is an air liaison element with a ground unit. It sends air support requests and gives terminal attack control.

c2-agency.title: Command and control agency

c2-agency.AgencyArea.description: An area selection is a reference to one planning area of the resource catalogue.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area that the agency covers.

common.description: Definitions for all openAIX documents are the identifiers, positions, geometry, units, time intervals and resource references that more than one type of document contains.
common.title: openAIX common resources

common.Activation.description: An activation is the time when a control measure is available. It is an interval, a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in an interval, or continuous activation.

continuous.description: The value is `true` when the control measure is active all the time, with no scheduled period in which it is not active.

common.AirspaceComponent.description: An airspace component is one part of an airspace in three dimensions, with a boundary, a floor and a ceiling. Each component adds a volume, subtracts a volume or intersects a volume, in sequence.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this component is available, in the time interval of the parent control measure. This field is optional.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal boundary of this component: points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator. A `geojson` geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.

id.description: This field identifies this component. Each component in its parent airspace has a different identifier.

lower_limit.description: This field gives the floor of this component: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

maximum_limit.description: This field gives the maximum limit of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `upper_limit`, it increases the ceiling. Each value keeps its reference.

minimum_limit.description: This field gives the minimum floor of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than `lower_limit`, it replaces the floor. To compare limits with different references, a consumer uses terrain or atmospheric data.

name.description: This field gives the name of this sector or shelf, for display.

operation.description: This field gives the operation of this component on the volume that the components before it make, as one of the enumerated values. The components operate in the sequence of the array, and the first component adds a volume.

upper_limit.description: This field gives the ceiling of this component: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.Altitude.description: An altitude is a vertical position with its unit and its reference: mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

reference.description: This field gives the vertical reference of the altitude, as one of the enumerated values. The value is mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the altitude: feet, metres or flight level, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the altitude, in the unit of `unit`.

common.Altitude.title: Altitude

common.AltitudeBlock.description: An altitude block is a vertical band between a floor and a ceiling. The floor can be the surface, and the ceiling can have no limit.

lower.description: This field gives the floor of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.

upper.description: This field gives the ceiling of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

common.AltitudeBlock.title: AltitudeBlock

common.Bearing.description: A bearing is a direction with its value and its north reference: true north or magnetic north. A magnetic bearing keeps the reference that its author gives. The declination is optional. When the declination is not available, a consumer should show that it cannot change the bearing to true north.

declination_deg.description: This field gives the magnetic declination that changes a bearing from true north to magnetic north, in degrees. This field is optional.

reference.description: This field gives the north reference of the bearing: true north or magnetic north, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the bearing, in degrees from 0 to less than 360.

common.BearingRange.description: A bearing range is a range of bearings from a start bearing clockwise to an end bearing.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the end of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the start of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

common.CasBrief.description: A close air support (CAS) brief is the data that the aircrew get for one CAS attack: the 9-line data of JP 3-09.3 and the mission-level data of the air tasking order (ATO). The ATO and the operation order (OPORD) use this one definition. A field that a use does not need stays out of the record. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Chapter V gives the check-in briefing and the CAS brief.

ato_mission.description: This field identifies the mission of the air tasking order (ATO) that receives the brief. The `orders` field of the operation order (OPORD) identifies the ATO.

check_in.description: This field gives the check-in data for the controller.

contact_points.description: This list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role `control`.

control_type.description: This field gives the type of terminal attack control, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.type_1: This value identifies type 1 terminal attack control, in which the controller sees the target and the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_2: This value identifies type 2 terminal attack control, in which the controller does not see the target or the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.type_3: This value identifies type 3 terminal attack control, in which the controller gives clearance for all attacks in an area.

controller.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that gives the brief.

controllers.description: This list contains the agencies and radio channels that control the close air support (CAS) for this brief.

danger_close.description: The value is `true` when the friendly forces are inside the danger-close distance of the weapons for the attack. The value is `false` when the friendly forces are outside that distance.

distance.description: This field gives the distance from the initial point to the target, as a length with its unit.

egress_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the egress point. The point shall have the role `egress`.

final_attack_headings.description: This list contains the ranges of final attack headings that the aircraft can use for the attack. Each range goes clockwise from its start bearing to its end bearing.

fire_support_measures.description: This list identifies the fire support coordination measures that apply to the close air support (CAS) mission.

friendly_direction.description: This field gives the direction from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

friendly_distance.description: This field gives the distance from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as a length with its unit.

friendly_lines.description: This list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.

friendly_marking.description: This field gives the means that marks the position of the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.

ground_scheme_summary.description: This field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.

hazards.description: This list contains the hazards in the target area that are not threats.

heading.description: This field gives the heading from the initial point to the target, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

holding.description: This list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.

holding_altitude.description: This field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.

id.description: This field identifies this close air support (CAS) brief. Each CAS brief in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this CAS brief.

initial_point.description: This field identifies the point that is the initial point of the attack. The point shall have the role `initial`.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the aircraft. Each point shall have the role `initial`.

laser_code.description: This field gives the code of the laser mark, as a laser code with its unit.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this brief.

laser_target_line.description: This field gives the laser target line, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

mark.description: This field gives the type of mark of the target, as one of the enumerated values.

marks.description: This list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.

method_of_attack.description: This field gives the method of attack, as one of the enumerated values.

offset_direction.description: This field gives the side of the line from the initial point to the target on which the aircraft fly the attack, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.left: The aircraft fly the attack to the left of the line from the initial point to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.right: The aircraft fly the attack to the right of the line from the initial point to the target.

remarks.description: This field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.

target.description: This field identifies the target of the resource catalogue that the brief is for.

target_description.description: This field gives the target description, as free text.

target_elevation.description: This field gives the elevation of the target, as an elevation with its unit.

target_position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the target, as latitude and longitude.

threats.description: This list identifies the threats of the resource catalogue that are a danger to the aircraft in the target area.

time_on_target.description: This field gives the time at which the weapons hit the target.

time_to_target_seconds.description: This field gives the time from the time of the brief to the time on target, in seconds.

common.CheckIn.description: A close air support (CAS) check-in is the data that the CAS aircrew gives to the controller at check-in. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Figure V-4 gives the check-in briefing.

abort_code.description: This field gives the abort code for the controller and the aircrew, as free text.

items.description: This list contains the parts of the check-in briefing that the aircrew gives.

x-enum-descriptions.abort_code: This value identifies the code that the aircrew uses to make sure that an abort call comes from the controller.
x-enum-descriptions.aircraft_number_and_type: This value identifies the quantity of aircraft in the flight and their aircraft type.
x-enum-descriptions.capabilities: This value identifies the sensors and the other capabilities of the aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.mission_number: This value identifies the mission number of the flight in the air tasking order (ATO).
x-enum-descriptions.ordnance: This value identifies the weapons on the aircraft, with the quantity of each.
x-enum-descriptions.position_and_altitude: This value identifies the position of the flight at this time, usually from a control point, and its altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.time_on_station: This value identifies the time that the aircraft can stay on station.

procedure.description: This field identifies the procedure that gives the check-in steps.

common.ClassificationLevel.description: A classification level is a security classification of the American government that the banner of an operation order (OPORD) can show.
common.ClassificationLevel.title: ClassificationLevel

common.Coalition.description: A coalition is the side of a record in the simulation: `blue`, `red` or `neutral`. It is simulator data, not real-world data.

common.ControlMeasure.description: A control measure is one openAIX control measure: a reference to one control measure contract, or an extension control measure with a namespace. The `type` field selects the contract.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which the extension control measure is available. The value is a schedule or a flag for continuous activation.

description.description: This field gives the information about this extension control measure and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the extension control measure: a position or a boundary. The geometry uses points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator, or a GeoJSON geometry (RFC 7946).

id.description: This field identifies this extension control measure. Other records and orders use it to refer to this extension control measure.

name.description: This field gives the name of this extension control measure, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this extension control measure, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this extension control measure. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: This field gives the type of the extension control measure, as a name with a namespace.

id.description: This field identifies the control measure of this selection.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a control measure selection. The value is `control_measure`.

common.ControllerContact.description: An agency channel is an agency for the aircrew, with its radio channels.

agency.description: This field identifies the agency or forward air controller that the aircrew speaks to. The value is the identifier of a command and control agency or of a forward air controller (FAC) of the resource catalogue.

alternate_channel.description: This field identifies the alternative radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency when the primary channel is not available.

channel.description: This field identifies the primary radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency.

common.DCSData.description: Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data is the data of a record for DCS. The `bindings` field contains the objects in a DCS mission that are this record or that show it. The other fields contain DCS values that are not objects of a mission.

alic_code.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft launcher interface computer (ALIC) code of the radar. The high-speed anti-radiation missile (HARM) of the DCS F-16C uses this code. Appendix B of the `DCS F-16C Early Access Guide` gives the codes.

angle_deg.description: This field gives the drawing angle from the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission, in degrees. This angle is not a true bearing or a magnetic bearing. Only a consumer with a correct adapter for DCS should use this angle to turn the shape.

bindings.description: This list contains the objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are this record or show it on the map. The record keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of these objects.

clsid.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifier (CLSID) of the load on the pylon. For a rack, the CLSID identifies the rack together with its stores.

clsids.description: This list contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifiers (CLSID) that agree with this store.

coalition.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) coalition of the record: `blue`, `red` or `neutral`, as one of the enumerated values. The coalition is the side of the record in the DCS mission.

label.description: This field gives the label of the pylon in the mission editor.

objects.description: This list contains the units, groups or static objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are parts of the aimpoint.

payload.description: This field identifies the load in the `UnitPayloads` file of the aircraft that agrees with this standard conventional load (SCL).

name.description: This field gives the name of the load in the `UnitPayloads` file.

task_ids.description: This list contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) task numbers of the load. The mission editor shows the load for these tasks, for example `31` for close air support (CAS).

unit_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the aircraft of the load.

projection.description: This field identifies the theatre projection of Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that gives the dimensions and the drawing angle.

pylon.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) pylon number of this station.

settings.description: This field contains the values of the pylon in the mission editor, such as the fuze values. The record keeps them for round trips.

type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the aircraft type, for example `F-16C_50`.

common.DCSObjectRef.description: A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object reference is a link to one object in a DCS mission. The record that contains this reference keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of this identifier.

angle_deg.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) angle of a point or circle drawing, in degrees. The angle is not a true bearing.

closed.description: The value is `true` when the line drawing is a closed shape. The value is `false` when the line drawing is an open line.

group_category.description: This field gives the class of the group: `airplane`, `helicopter`, `vehicle`, `ship` or `train`, as one of the enumerated values.

icon.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) identifier of the icon file.
