kind.description: This field gives the type of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, as one of the enumerated values. The types are units, groups, static objects, `scenery` objects, airbases, parking stands, drawings and trigger zones.

layer.description: This field gives the drawing layer in the mission editor, such as `Blue` or `Author`.

line_mode.description: This field gives the mode of a line drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.

mission_id.description: This field identifies the mission in which a consumer resolves names and number identifiers. This field is optional.

name.description: This field gives the name of this Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, for display.

native_fields.description: This field contains the attributes from Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that have no typed field. The record keeps them for round trips. A typed field for identifiers, geometry or style shall not go in this object.

object_id.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) number that identifies the object in the mission.

polygon_mode.description: This field gives the mode of a polygon drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.

primitive_type.description: This field gives the drawing primitive in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values. The value is a polygon, a line, a text box or an icon.

style.description: This field contains display attributes from the mission editor, when they are known. The geometry does not change with them.

color.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) colour of the line or text in the format `0xRRGGBBAA`. The format gives the red value, green value, blue value and alpha.

fill_color.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) fill colour in the format `0xRRGGBBAA`. The format gives the red value, green value, blue value and alpha.

font_size.description: This field gives the font size of the text in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS).

thickness.description: This field gives the width of the line in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS).

visible.description: The value is `true` when the drawing shows on the map. The value is `false` when the drawing does not show on the map.

text.description: This field gives the text of a text box drawing, as free text.

unit_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the unit or the static object, when known.

zone_type.description: This field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type of the trigger zone, as one of the enumerated values. The value `circle` is zone type 0, and the value `quad` is zone type 2.

common.DateTime.description: A date-time is an RFC 3339 date-time with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) designator or an offset from UTC, such as `2026-10-02T06:00:00Z`.

common.DocumentRef.description: A document reference is a document that a record refers to. Consumers do not get the document automatically through a network.

id.description: This field identifies the document that the record refers to.

path.description: This field gives the file path of the document.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the document.

section.description: This field gives the part of the document that the record refers to, such as a section or a paragraph.

title.description: This field gives the title of the document.

common.DocumentRef.title: DocumentRef

reference.description: This field gives the vertical reference of the elevation. The value is always `MSL`.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the elevation: feet or metres, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the elevation, in the unit of `unit`.

sim.description: This field contains the simulator data of the record, with the simulator identifier as the key.

common.Frequency.description: A frequency is a radio frequency in kilohertz or megahertz. The modulation is amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM). The modulation and the radio band are optional.

band.description: This field gives the radio band of the frequency, as one of the enumerated values. The band shall agree with the value of the frequency. The limits are 2 to 30 MHz for high frequency (HF), and 30 to 88 MHz for frequency modulation (FM). The limits are 108 to 174 MHz for very high frequency (VHF), and 225 to 400 MHz for ultra high frequency (UHF).

x-enum-descriptions.fm: This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band with frequency modulation (FM) that army radios use, from 30 to 88 MHz.
x-enum-descriptions.hf: This value identifies the high frequency (HF) band, from 3 to 30 MHz, for radio communication at long range.
x-enum-descriptions.uhf: This value identifies the ultra high frequency (UHF) band of the aircraft radios of armed forces, from 225 to 400 MHz.
x-enum-descriptions.vhf: This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band of aircraft radios, from 118 to 137 MHz.

modulation.description: This field gives the modulation of the radio frequency: amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM), as one of the enumerated values. This field is optional.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the frequency: kilohertz or megahertz, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the frequency, in the unit of `unit`.

common.FriendlyMarking.description: A friendly marking is the means that marks the position of the friendly forces for the aircrew.

x-enum-descriptions.chemical_light: This value identifies a chemical light stick that gives light for a short time, usually at night.
x-enum-descriptions.flare: This value identifies a pyrotechnic flare that burns bright at the friendly position.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_strobe: This value identifies an infrared strobe light that aircrew with night vision devices can see.
x-enum-descriptions.mirror: This value identifies a mirror that reflects the light of the sun.
x-enum-descriptions.panel: This value identifies a panel with a bright colour on the ground.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies coloured smoke from a grenade or a canister at the friendly position.
x-enum-descriptions.strobe: This value identifies a visible strobe light that flashes at the friendly position.

common.GeoJSONLineString.description: A GeoJSON line string is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `LineString`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the positions of the line string, in order. Each item is a GeoJSON position.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `LineString`.

common.GeoJSONLinearRing.description: A GeoJSON linear ring is a closed sequence of four or more positions. The first position and the last position shall be the same.

common.GeoJSONMultiPolygon.description: A GeoJSON multipolygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `MultiPolygon`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the polygons of the multipolygon. Each polygon is a list of linear rings, as in a GeoJSON polygon.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `MultiPolygon`.

common.GeoJSONPoint.description: A GeoJSON point is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `Point`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This field gives the GeoJSON position of the point: longitude first, then latitude.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `Point`.

common.GeoJSONPolygon.description: A GeoJSON polygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type `Polygon`, as in RFC 7946.

bbox.description: This list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.

coordinates.description: This list contains the linear rings of the polygon. The first ring is the outer boundary; the other rings are holes.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON `Polygon`.

common.GeoJSONPosition.description: A GeoJSON position is a longitude and a latitude in WGS 84 decimal degrees, in this sequence. A third number, the height, is optional. This sequence is the opposite of a geographic point.

common.GeoPoint.description: A geographic point is a position in WGS 84 decimal degrees. An adapter is necessary for the Cartesian coordinates of a simulator.

latitude.description: This field gives the latitude north of the equator, in decimal degrees. A south latitude is a negative value.

longitude.description: This field gives the longitude east of Greenwich, in decimal degrees. A west longitude is a negative value.

common.GeoPoint.title: GeoPoint

common.Geometry_circle.description: A circle geometry is a horizontal disc with a centre and a radius.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the circle, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a circle geometry. The value is `circle`.

radius.description: This field gives the horizontal distance from the centre to the boundary, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_corridor.description: A corridor geometry is a route centreline with a total lateral width.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a corridor geometry. The value is `corridor`.

one_way.description: The value is `true` when aircraft fly the corridor only in the sequence of its points. The value is `false` when aircraft fly the corridor in the two directions.

points.description: This list contains the geographic positions of the centreline, in order. The first position is the start.

width.description: This field gives the total lateral width of the corridor, with the centreline at its centre, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_description.description: A `description` geometry is a text that gives a geographic position or an area, with no coordinates.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a `description` geometry. The value is `description`.

text.description: This field gives the geographic position or area, as free text.

common.Geometry_ellipse.description: An ellipse geometry is an ellipse with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in `extensions.sim.dcs`.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the ellipse, as latitude and longitude.

east_radius_m.description: This field gives the east radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a ellipse geometry. The value is `ellipse`.

north_radius_m.description: This field gives the north radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

common.Geometry_figure_eight.description: A figure-eight geometry is a figure-eight flight pattern with an anchor, an axis, a leg length and a turn radius.

axis.description: This field gives the direction of the axis of the flight pattern from its anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a figure-eight geometry. The value is `figure_eight`.

leg_length.description: This field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.

point.description: This field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the flight pattern, as latitude and longitude.

turn_radius.description: This field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_geojson_line.description: A GeoJSON line geometry is a line as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `LineString` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_geojson_point.description: A GeoJSON point geometry is a point as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `Point` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_geojson_polygon.description: A GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon geometry is a polygon or multipolygon as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

geometry.description: This field contains the GeoJSON `Polygon` or `MultiPolygon` object.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is `geojson`.

common.Geometry_line.description: A line geometry is a sequence of geographic positions that makes an open line.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a line geometry. The value is `line`.

points.description: This list contains the geographic positions of the open line, in order. The first position is the start.

common.Geometry_path.description: A path geometry is an open line of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence. It does not close into an area.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path geometry. The value is `path`.

segments.description: This list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the path. A straight segment that follows a straight segment shall start at its end.

end.description: This field gives the geographic position of the end of the straight segment, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

start.description: This field gives the geographic position of the start of the straight segment, as latitude and longitude.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the arc, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the end of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a path segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

radius.description: This field gives the radius of the arc, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the start of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the arc from its start to its end, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `left`, the arc turns to the left side, and with `right`, it turns to the right side.

common.Geometry_point.description: A point geometry is one geographic position.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a point geometry. The value is `point`.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.

common.Geometry_polyarc.description: A polyarc geometry is a horizontal boundary of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a polyarc geometry. The value is `polyarc`.

segments.description: This list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the boundary.

end.description: This field gives the geographic position of the end of the boundary segment, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a boundary segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

start.description: This field gives the geographic position of the start of the boundary segment, as latitude and longitude.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the arc, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the end of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a boundary segment. The value is `line` for a straight segment and `arc` for an arc.

radius.description: This field gives the radius of the arc, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing from the centre to the start of the arc, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the arc from its start to its end, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `left`, the arc turns to the left side, and with `right`, it turns to the right side.

common.Geometry_polygon.description: A polygon geometry is a closed horizontal boundary. The first ring is the external boundary, and the next rings are holes.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a polygon geometry. The value is `polygon`.

rings.description: This list contains the closed rings of positions, in order. The external boundary is first, and the holes come after it.

common.Geometry_racetrack.description: A racetrack geometry is a racetrack with an anchor, an outbound radial, a turn direction and a straight-leg length.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a racetrack geometry. The value is `racetrack`.

leg_length.description: This field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.

point.description: This field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

radial.description: This field gives the outbound bearing from the anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference. The reference is always given: true north or magnetic north. The reciprocal course is the course of the inbound leg.

turn_radius.description: This field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

common.Geometry_rectangle.description: A rectangle geometry is a rectangle with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in `extensions.sim.dcs`.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the rectangle, as latitude and longitude.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

height_m.description: This field gives the height before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a rectangle geometry. The value is `rectangle`.

width_m.description: This field gives the width before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

common.Geometry_sector.description: A sector geometry is a horizontal sector with a centre, a start bearing, an end bearing, and an inner and an outer radius.

center.description: This field gives the geographic position of the centre of the sector, as latitude and longitude.

end_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing of the second side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

inner_radius.description: This field gives the inner radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a sector geometry. The value is `sector`.

outer_radius.description: This field gives the outer radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.

start_bearing.description: This field gives the bearing of the first side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

common.Geometry_track_racetrack.description: A track racetrack geometry is a racetrack with two end anchors, a lateral width and a turn direction.

a.description: This field gives the geographic position of the first end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

b.description: This field gives the geographic position of the second end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a track racetrack geometry. The value is `track_racetrack`.

turns.description: This field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.

width.description: This field gives the horizontal width of the racetrack, as a length with its unit.

common.Geometry_vertical.description: A vertical geometry is a coordination level, or the two values of a traverse level. The values of a traverse level are a height above the ground and an altitude above mean sea level.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a vertical geometry. The value is `vertical`.

level.description: This field gives the altitude of the coordination level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude of the traverse level above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

height.description: This field gives the height of the traverse level above the ground, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a vertical geometry. The value is `vertical`.

common.Hazard.description: A hazard is a danger to the aircraft in the target area that is not a threat.

description.description: This field gives the hazard, as free text.

kind.description: This field gives the type of hazard, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.friendly_aircraft: This value identifies other friendly aircraft in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies friendly artillery, mortar or naval gun fire in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.obstruction: This value identifies an obstruction, such as a tower or a mast.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a hazard that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.terrain: This value identifies high ground in or near the attack run.
x-enum-descriptions.weather: This value identifies a dangerous weather condition in the target area.
x-enum-descriptions.wires: This value identifies wires or cables in the air.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the hazard, as latitude and longitude.

common.LaserCode.description: A laser code is a code of four digits for the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of a laser, from `1111` to `1788`. The second digit is 1 to 7, and the last two digits are 1 to 8.

common.Length.description: A length is a horizontal distance or dimension with its unit: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the length: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the length, in the unit of `unit`.

author.description: This field gives the name of the author of the document.

classification.description: This field gives the security classification of the document, as one of the enumerated values.

distribution.description: This list contains the addressees that receive the document.

id.description: This field identifies this document. Other records and orders use it to refer to this document.

issued_at.description: This field gives the time of issue of the document.

issuing_unit.description: This field gives the name of the unit that publishes the document.

operation.description: This field gives the name of the operation that the document is for.

references.description: This list contains the documents that this document refers to.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the document.

supersedes.description: This field identifies the document that this document replaces.

title.description: This field gives the title of the document.

common.Offset.description: An offset is a number of minutes from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it. The value can be less than zero.

offset_minutes.description: This field gives the time from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it, in minutes. A negative value is before the start of the period.

common.Offset.title: Offset

common.Period.description: A period is a time interval between two absolute date-times in the RFC 3339 format.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.

common.Period.title: Period

common.PinnedRef.description: A pinned reference is a dependency on a local document that consumers examine by identifier and revision.

id.description: This field identifies the local document of this dependency.

path.description: This field gives the file path of the local document.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the local document. Consumers examine this revision.

common.PinnedRef.title: PinnedRef

common.PointLocation.description: A point location is a geographic point, a location in free text, or the two.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.

position_description.description: This field gives the location, as free text. The text is for a location without accurate coordinates, or it gives more information about the coordinates.

common.Pressure.description: A pressure is an atmospheric pressure with its unit: inches of mercury or hectopascals.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the pressure: inches of mercury or hectopascals, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.inHg: The pressure is in inches of mercury.

value.description: This field gives the value of the pressure, in the unit of `unit`.

activities.description: This list identifies the flight operations that use this radio assignment. Each identifier shall refer to an item of `activities` of the flight. When the list is not given, the assignment is for the complete mission.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that this assignment uses.

preset.description: This field gives the preset number of the radio channel on the radio of the aircraft.

purpose.description: This field gives the operation or objective of this radio assignment, as free text.

radio.description: This field gives the radio of the aircraft that uses the channel, such as `UHF` or `VHF`, as free text.

id.description: This field identifies the external resource catalogue.

revision.description: This field gives the revision of the external resource catalogue.

common.RunwayDesignator.description: A runway designator is the magnetic heading of the runway in units of 10 degrees, from `01` to `36`. A suffix can follow: `L`, `R` or `C` for left, right or centre, or `W` for water. Other suffixes are `S` for short take-off and landing (STOL), `G` for glider and `U` for ultralight aircraft.

common.ScheduledWindow.description: A scheduled window is a time interval between two absolute date-times, with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in it.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.

schedule.description: This field gives the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in the interval.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.

common.SimData.description: Simulator data is the data of a record for each simulator, with the simulator identifier as the key, for example `dcs`. The other fields of the record do not change with a simulator. The Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data has fixed fields, and the data of a different simulator is an object with no fixed fields.

dcs.description: This field contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data of the record.

common.Speed.description: A speed is a speed with its unit: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the speed: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour, as one of the enumerated values.

value.description: This field gives the value of the speed, in the unit of `unit`.

common.TACAN.description: A Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) is the channel, band and identifier of a TACAN station.

band.description: This field gives the band of the channel: `X` or `Y`, as one of the enumerated values.

channel.description: This field gives the channel number of the station, from 1 to 126.

common.TACAN.title: TACAN

common.TargetMark.description: A target mark is the means that marks a target for the aircrew. The close air support (CAS) briefs of the air tasking order (ATO) and the operation order (OPORD) use this one list of values.

x-enum-descriptions.illumination: This value identifies a mark from illumination ammunition above or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.indirect_fire: This value identifies a mark from artillery, mortar or naval gun fire.
x-enum-descriptions.infrared_pointer: This value identifies a mark from an infrared pointer. Aircrew with night vision devices can see it on the target.
x-enum-descriptions.laser: This value identifies a mark from a laser designator, which the seeker of the weapon or the targeting pod of the aircraft detects.
x-enum-descriptions.smoke: This value identifies a mark from smoke ammunition at or near the target.
x-enum-descriptions.talk_on: This value identifies a talk-on, in which the controller tells the aircrew how to find the target by voice.
x-enum-descriptions.tracer: This value identifies a mark from tracer rounds, which show the line of fire to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.white_phosphorus: This value identifies a mark from white phosphorus ammunition at or near the target.

common.VerticalLimit.description: A vertical limit is a floor or a ceiling: an altitude with its reference, the surface, or no limit. The surface is below all altitudes, and the value `unlimited` is above all altitudes.

surface.description: The value is `true` when the limit is the surface. The value is always `true`. The surface is below all altitudes.

unlimited.description: The value is `true` when the limit has no maximum. The value is always `true`. This limit is above all altitudes.

end_day_offset.description: This field gives the day on which the period stops, as one of the enumerated values. With the value `0`, the period stops on its start day, and with `1`, it stops on the next day.

end_time.description: This field gives the time of the end of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as `HH:MM:SS`. The period does not include the end time.

start_time.description: This field gives the time of the start of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as `HH:MM:SS`. The period includes the start time.

weekdays.description: This list contains the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) weekdays on which this period starts.

common.WeeklySchedule.description: A schedule for each week is the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) times in the week when something is available, in the interval that contains it. The intervals in `exclusions` are not part of the schedule.

exclusions.description: This list contains the time intervals with absolute date-times that the schedule subtracts from its periods.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval that the schedule does not include. The value is an absolute date-time.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval that the schedule does not include. The value is an absolute date-time.

periods.description: This list contains the time intervals in each week.

time_reference.description: This field gives the time reference of the schedule. The value is always `UTC`.

common.Window.description: A window is a time interval with limits that are absolute date-times or offsets from the period of the order that contains it.

end.description: This field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.

start.description: This field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.

common.Window.title: Window

ext-kneeboard.title: Kneeboard extension
ext-kneeboard.description: The `org.opord-builder.kneeboard` extension: kneeboard cards, or overrides of the card built from an ATO flight. On a flight, a card with no `flight_callsign` applies to that flight.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardATCEntry.description: Single ATC / control agency frequency entry.

name.description: Agency name (e.g. 'MARSHAL', 'TOWER', 'DEPARTURE', 'AI CV CONTROLLER').

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCard.description:
A single kneeboard card for DCS World (768×1024 PNG) or print.

Captures the tactical data a pilot needs on the knee: flight lineup,
comms plan, fuel plan, objectives, tanker info, and ATC frequencies.
Values can reference OPORD/FRAGO variables via Jinja2 interpolation.

title.description: Card title / header line (defaults to flight_callsign if blank).

positions.description: Aircraft positions in the flight (lead, wingmen).

timing.description: Package time on target and push.

weather.description: One line of weather for the mission: clouds, visibility and surface wind of the forecast that covers it.

notes.description: Freeform notes.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCommsPhase.description: Radio assignments for one mission phase.

comm1.description: COMM 1 radio assignment for this phase.

comm2.description: COMM 2 radio assignment for this phase.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardCommsPlan.description: Complete communications plan for the kneeboard card.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardPosition.description: Single aircraft position within a flight.

number.description: Position in flight (1 = lead, 2 = wingman, etc.).
Steerpoint number: the route point's number, else its position in the route from 1.

name.description: Name of the route point.

altitude.description: Altitude of the route point, with unit and reference.

action.description: Flight phase at the point (ingress, egress, hold, ...).

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardTACAN.description: TACAN channel plan for the flight.

ext-kneeboard.KneeboardTiming.description: Package timing figures for the flight.

ext-measure.title: Measure extension
ext-measure.description: The `org.opord-builder.measure` extension on a control measure: the catalogue code of a measure whose type has none (AXIS, CFZ, SFA, RFZ, SAR, DZ/LZ/PZ, MRR), and the authoring fields of a data-source entry that the typed measure does not carry.

code.description: The control-measure code the authoring model used; only on a measure of type `org.opord-builder.measure`.

extra.description: Authoring field -> value for the fields of the original entry that have no typed home in the measure or that do not read back exactly from it.

fac.description: A forward air controller (FAC) is a record of a FAC, a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)). It contains the role, the platform, the communications and the control functions of the controller.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

callsign.description: This field gives the radio call sign of the controller, as free text.

channels.description: This list identifies the radio channels that the controller uses.

coordinate_source.description: This field gives the method that the controller uses to get target coordinates, as one of the enumerated values. The value is not a type of target location error.

x-enum-descriptions.exact: This value identifies accurate coordinates from the simulator.
x-enum-descriptions.lrf: This value identifies coordinates from a laser rangefinder at a known observer position.
x-enum-descriptions.visual: This value identifies a visual estimate by the controller.

default_laser_code.description: This field gives the laser code that the controller uses when the brief gives no other code, as a laser code with its unit.

egress_points.description: This list identifies the egress points that the controller gives to aircraft. Each one refers to a point with the role egress, gate or fix.

equipment.description: This list contains the equipment items that the controller or the observer team has. When an item is not in the list, the list does not add or remove that equipment.

available.description: The value is `true` when this equipment is available for the operation in the plan.

horizontal_accuracy.description: This field gives the horizontal precision of the equipment that its data gives, as a length with its unit.

id.description: This field identifies this equipment item. Other records and orders use it to refer to this equipment item.

kind.description: This field gives the type of equipment, as one of the enumerated values.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes that the equipment can use.

max_range.description: This field gives the maximum range at which the equipment operates, as a length with its unit.

name.description: This field gives the name of this equipment item, for display. The name is the identification or the type of the equipment.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this equipment, such as limits, supply condition or employment, as free text.

quantity.description: This field gives the number of items of this equipment that are available.

vertical_accuracy.description: This field gives the vertical precision of the equipment that its data gives, as a length with its unit.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record. The data in this field is for one consumer. The controller record keeps the data that all consumers can use. Examples are the identification, the equipment and the functions of the controller.

id.description: This field identifies this controller. Other records and orders use it to refer to this controller.

initial_points.description: This list identifies the initial points that the controller uses for attack briefs. Each one refers to a point with the role initial or fix.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a forward air controller.

laser_codes.description: This list contains the laser codes that the designators of the controller can use.

platform.description: This field gives the platform of the controller: on the ground (`ground`) or in an aircraft (`airborne`), as one of the enumerated values.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the controller, as latitude and longitude.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.

role.description: This field gives the qualification of the controller, as one of the enumerated values. The controller is a forward air controller (FAC), a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)).

smoke_color.description: This field gives the colour of the smoke that identifies targets or friendly positions, as one of the enumerated values.

terminal_control.description: This list contains the types of terminal attack control that the controller may give.

fac.title: Forward air controller

localizer.description: A localizer is the transmitter of an instrument landing system (ILS) that shows the lateral position of the aircraft in relation to the course. The record has its frequency, its course and, when the ILS has one, its glide slope.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield of the localizer. When the airfield has a list of its localizers, the list shall include this localizer.

course.description: This field gives the front course of the localizer, as a bearing with its unit and reference. A magnetic course includes the station declination, which is more than zero for east.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the localizer frequency: megahertz (`MHz`).

frequency.description: This field gives the frequency of the localizer, as a frequency with its unit. The unit is megahertz.

glide_slope.description: This field gives the glide slope transmitter for the same runway, when the runway has one.

id.description: This field identifies this localizer. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this localizer.

ident.description: This field identifies this localizer as the station transmits it in Morse code. An example is `IDQQ`.

ils_category.description: This field gives the instrument landing system (ILS) Category of the localizer, as one of the enumerated values. A localizer without a glide slope does not have this field.

x-enum-descriptions.I: This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height of 200 feet or more.
x-enum-descriptions.II: This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height from 100 feet to less than 200 feet.
x-enum-descriptions.III: This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height of less than 100 feet, or with no decision height.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a localizer record. The value selects this navigation contract.

name.description: This field gives the name of this localizer, for display.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the localizer antenna, as latitude and longitude.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this localizer as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this localizer. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

runway.description: This field gives the designator of the runway of the localizer.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

threshold_crossing_height.description: This field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the glide slope, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the glide slope above the landing threshold.

localizer.title: Localizer

angle_deg.description: This field gives the angle between the glide path and a horizontal line, in degrees.

elevation.description: This field gives the elevation of the glide slope antenna above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the glide slope antenna, as latitude and longitude.

measure-aca.description: An airspace coordination area (ACA) is a block or corridor of airspace above a target area. In it, friendly aircraft are reasonably safe from friendly surface fires. The airspace control authority establishes a formal airspace coordination area on the request of a component. It has a minimum altitude, a maximum altitude, a baseline, a width on each side of the baseline and effective times. In an informal airspace coordination area, time, lateral distance or altitude keeps aircraft and surface fires apart. A battalion or higher headquarters gives approval for it.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

aca_kind.description: This field gives the type of airspace coordination area (ACA): `formal` or `informal`, as one of the enumerated values. In openAIX, an ACA of the type `formal` is a volume, and an ACA of the type `informal` gives only its method of separation. The airspace control authority makes an ACA of the type `formal` when a component sends a request for it. It has altitudes, a baseline, a width and the times when it is active. In an ACA of the type `informal`, time, lateral distance or altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires. A battalion or a higher unit gives the approval for an ACA of the type `informal`.

x-enum-descriptions.formal: The airspace control authority makes the airspace coordination area (ACA) when a component sends a request for it. It has a minimum and a maximum altitude, a baseline, a width and the times when it is active (JP 3-09, Appendix A, 5.d).
x-enum-descriptions.informal: Time, lateral distance or altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires. A battalion or a higher unit gives the approval for it (JP 3-09, Appendix A, 5.d).

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace coordination area is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace coordination area.

components.description: This list contains the airspace components of the coordination volume. A formal airspace coordination area (ACA) is usually a corridor component along its baseline, between the minimum and maximum altitudes.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace coordination area.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace coordination area has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this airspace coordination area and its local conditions, as free text.

establishing_authority.description: This field identifies the authority that set this airspace coordination area.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airspace coordination area. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace coordination area.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airspace coordination area, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace coordination area, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace coordination area, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace coordination area. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace coordination area.

separation.description: This field gives the method of separation between aircraft and surface fires in an informal airspace coordination area (ACA), as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.altitude: Altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires.
x-enum-descriptions.combined: This value identifies separation by time, lateral distance and altitude together.
x-enum-descriptions.lateral: Lateral distance gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires.
x-enum-descriptions.time: Aircraft and surface fires use the area at different times.

type.description: The value identifies this record as an airspace coordination area. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

measure-aca.title: Airspace coordination area

measure-aor.description: An area of responsibility (AOR) is the geographic area of a commander, in which that commander has the authority to plan and conduct operations. The airspace control area (ACAR) can be the same as the AOR of a regional commander. It can be the same as the joint operations area of the commander of the joint force command. The ACAR can also be smaller than the AOR, because of limits of nations or of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), or larger. The `responsible_agency` and `gates` fields are openAIX planning fields.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this area of responsibility is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

description.description: This field gives the information about this area of responsibility and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

gates.description: This list identifies the entry and exit gates of this area.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the area of responsibility: a polygon, a circle, a rectangle, an ellipse or a GeoJSON polygon.

id.description: This field identifies this area of responsibility. Other records and orders use it to refer to this area of responsibility.

name.description: This field gives the name of this area of responsibility, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this area of responsibility, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this area of responsibility. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

responsible_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls this area.

type.description: The value identifies this record as an area of responsibility. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

measure-aor.title: Area of responsibility

measure-area.description: A surface fire support or manoeuvre area is an area on the ground in two dimensions, with no vertical limits. The code `NFA` prevents fires and their effects, and with the code `FFA`, fires can occur without more coordination. With the code `RFA`, fires that do not obey the restrictions of the area can occur only with coordination. The code `EA` identifies the engagement area that the commander plans, and `AOA` identifies the amphibious objective area. The codes `OBJ`, `BP`, `AA`, `NAI` and `TAI` identify ground manoeuvre graphics. The code `FSA` identifies a sea area for fire support ships.

x-enum-descriptions.AA: An assembly area (AA) is an area where a unit makes its preparation for an operation.
x-enum-descriptions.AOA: An amphibious objective area (AOA) is a geographical area that the initiating directive gives for command and control. It contains the objectives that the amphibious task force is to make safe.
x-enum-descriptions.AXIS: An axis of advance is the general area through which the bulk of the combat power of a unit must move. A commander uses it to make the force bypass locations that could delay it. It also shows that the force does not have to clear all of the assigned area. It shows a unit in an encirclement, exploitation or pursuit that it must move quickly toward an objective. Bypass criteria go with it. Any manoeuvre echelon can use one. The axis of a subordinate unit stays inside the axis of its higher headquarters.
x-enum-descriptions.BP: A battle position (BP) is a defence location in the direction of a likely enemy avenue of approach. It is not an area of operations.
x-enum-descriptions.CFZ: A critical friendly zone is an area of friendly weapons locating radar coverage that a commander designates. It is critical to the protection of an asset. The loss of that asset would seriously jeopardize the mission. The zone needs weapons locating radar coverage and attack assets that can give counterfire. The supporting field artillery unit puts enemy indirect fire that the radar acquires into the zone ahead of all other counterfire targets.
x-enum-descriptions.EA: An engagement area (EA) is an area of ground manoeuvre control in which the commander plans to contain and destroy an enemy force. The commander uses the massed effects of all available weapons and the systems that help them. Close air support is an example. The commander may divide the area into smaller areas for subordinate units.
x-enum-descriptions.FFA: A free-fire area (FFA) is a permissive area for fires. Any weapon system may fire into it without further coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). Joint fires can occur more quickly in it, and it helps aircraft jettison munitions. Only the commander with jurisdiction, usually at division or higher, may establish it.
x-enum-descriptions.FSA: A fire support area (FSA) is a sea manoeuvre area that the naval force commander gives to fire support ships. From this area, the ships supply gunfire support to an amphibious operation. The officer in tactical command establishes it.
x-enum-descriptions.NAI: A named area of interest (NAI) is a geospatial area, or a systems node or link, where forces get information for a specified information requirement. This information usually shows enemy and adversary courses of action.
x-enum-descriptions.NFA: A no-fire area (NFA) is a restrictive area that prohibits joint fires and their effects into the area. The establishing headquarters (HQ) may give approval for fires into it, one mission at a time. When an enemy force in the area engages a friendly force, the friendly force may use minimal force in self-defence. A unit of any size may establish an NFA.
x-enum-descriptions.OBJ: An objective (OBJ) is a location for the orientation of operations, the phases of operations, changes of direction and unity of effort. It can be a terrain objective or a force objective.
x-enum-descriptions.RFA: A restrictive fire area (RFA) is an area with special restrictions on joint fires. Units do not fire joint fires that are more than these restrictions, or that have such effects, without coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). A manoeuvre battalion or higher usually establishes it. Restrictive fire areas can also be on-call areas that units prepare before the operation.
x-enum-descriptions.TAI: A target area of interest (TAI) is a geographical area where friendly forces find and engage high-value targets.

The code `CL` is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) coordination level, and the code `CA` is the coordinating altitude of JP 3-52. The record can identify the agencies that control the airspace below and above the level. The lateral limits come from text or from unit boundaries, not from this record.

x-enum-descriptions.CA: A coordinating altitude (CA) is an airspace coordinating measure that uses altitude to separate users and as the transition between different airspace control elements. Airspace users should coordinate with these elements before they fly or fire through it.
x-enum-descriptions.CL: A coordination level (CL) is one altitude or height that sets airspace control responsibilities. The CL deconflicts airspace users, and this is its primary function. It usually divides the users above it from the users below it.

measure-fire-support-line.description: A fire support line is one of four lines for the coordination of fires. The headquarters of a ground force, of an amphibious force or of the two forces together sets it. On the far side of a coordinated fire line (CFL), in the boundaries of its headquarters, standard indirect fires can occur without more coordination. Other forces should coordinate their fires on the far side of a fire support coordination line (FSCL) with its commander. A restrictive fire line (RFL) between friendly forces that come together prevents fires and their effects across it without coordination. Between a battlefield coordination line (BCL) and the FSCL, Marine aircraft can attack surface targets without approval from the ground combat element (GCE) commander.

x-enum-descriptions.BCL: A battlefield coordination line (BCL) is a fire support coordination measure of the Marine Corps. Between it and the fire support coordination line (FSCL), Marine air-ground task force (MAGTF) aviation quickly attacks surface targets of opportunity. The approval of the ground combat element (GCE) commander of the area where the targets are is not necessary. The MAGTF commander establishes the BCL. An airspace coordination area (ACA) or a kill box usually includes the area between the BCL and the FSCL.
x-enum-descriptions.CFL: A coordinated fire line (CFL) is a line that a land headquarters sets. Beyond this line, conventional indirect surface fire support means may fire at any time without further coordination. This is applicable only in the boundaries of the establishing headquarters.
x-enum-descriptions.FSCL: A fire support coordination line (FSCL) is a line in the area of operations (AO) for the coordination of fires by other force elements. A land or amphibious force commander establishes it. These fires can have an effect on the current and planned operations of that commander. Other force elements should coordinate these fires with that commander. The establishing commander should coordinate the line with the affected commanders.
x-enum-descriptions.RFL: A restrictive fire line (RFL) is a line between converging friendly forces, of which one or both may move. It prohibits joint fires and the effects of joint fires across the line without coordination with the affected force. Its function is to prevent friendly fire and the duplication of engagements by the converging forces. The commander common to the converging forces establishes it.

This identification shows that the aircraft are friendly. This range makes sure that the maritime force does not mistake the aircraft for hostile. The officer in tactical command sets it. The range moves with the maritime force. A record can give a circle geometry for display at a specified time.

measure-kb.description: A kill box (KB) is a three-dimensional reference system that gives good coordination and control at the correct time, and helps attacks occur quickly. For dynamic targeting operations, it is a permissive fire support coordination measure (FSCM). It decreases the coordination requirements, thus it gives the maximum effects of airpower. Attacks in it occur quickly with less coordination, in the limits of the law of armed conflict (LOAC) and the rules of engagement (ROE). The `killbox_kind` field gives the type, a blue kill box or a purple kill box, from FM 3-09 (2024), paragraph B-19. The firing status `open` or `closed` comes from the assignments in the airspace control order (ACO), not from this record.

A blue kill box lets aircraft attack surface targets, and it starts at the surface or at its coordinating altitude. A purple kill box also lets surface units fire at surface targets, and it has an altitude floor.

The kill box extends from the surface to a ceiling altitude. Units coordinate indirect fires that hit in it or go through it. The coordination is with the airspace control element, the kill box coordinator or the aircrew on station.
x-enum-descriptions.purple: Air-to-surface attacks, surface-to-surface fires and subsurface-to-surface fires in the kill box occur with no further coordination with the area of operations (AO) commander. The kill box has an altitude floor, and aircraft do not fly below the floor. Indirect fires that stay below the floor need no further coordination.

The line is the forward line of own troops (FLOT), the forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) or a ground manoeuvre graphic. These graphics are the phase line, the boundary, the limit of advance (LOA), the line of departure (LD) and the line of contact (LC). Other lines show where friendly aircraft set their identification, friend or foe (IFF) equipment to off or on.

x-enum-descriptions.BOUNDARY: A boundary is a line that delineates surface areas for the coordination and deconfliction of operations. These operations are between units, formations or areas that are next to each other.
x-enum-descriptions.FEBA: A forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) is the foremost limits of the areas of the ground combat units. It does not include the areas of the covering or screening forces. It helps to coordinate fire support, the positions of forces and manoeuvre.
x-enum-descriptions.FLOT: A forward line of own troops (FLOT) is a line that shows the most forward positions of friendly forces at a given time. This is applicable to any kind of military operation.
x-enum-descriptions.IFFOFF: An identification, friend or foe switch-off line (IFFOFF) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft stop the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft stop their IFF transponder at this line, before they go to the target.
x-enum-descriptions.IFFON: An identification, friend or foe switch-on line (IFFON) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft start the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft start their IFF transponder again at this line, after the mission.
x-enum-descriptions.LC: A line of contact (LC) is a general trace that delineates the location where friendly and enemy forces engage each other. In the defence, it is frequently the same as the forward line of own troops (FLOT). In an offensive operation, it can be the same as the line of departure (LD).
x-enum-descriptions.LD: A line of departure (LD) is a line in land warfare that coordinates the departure of attack elements.
x-enum-descriptions.LOA: A limit of advance (LOA) is a phase line that controls the forward progress of the attack. The attack unit does not advance its elements or assets across this line. The unit may move its security forces up to the line.
x-enum-descriptions.PL: A phase line (PL) is an identifiable feature in the operational area, for the control and coordination of military operations. A phase line is not a boundary, unless the commander designates it as a boundary.

measure-mez.description: A missile engagement zone (MEZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in air and missile defence, normally reserved for engagements by surface-to-air missile (SAM) weapon systems. It is an air defence measure. In maritime zone coordination, it is together with the fighter engagement zone (FEZ) and the joint engagement zone (JEZ). Its limits are a sector, an altitude, a range and bearing from a point of origin, or a mixture of these. Aircraft should coordinate before they go into it. Its centre is on the bearing of the target, and its range extends to the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile (SAM). The arc has its centre on the firing unit, and its axis is the bearing of the target. Its width is 10 degrees by default, and its range is the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile.

Only a published visual flight rules (VFR) route (`VFRRTE`) can have no vertical limits. The type code gives the task of the route, and it tells if the route has air traffic services. runway.description: This field gives the designator of the runway end, such as `31`.

type.description: This field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.

x-enum-descriptions.AIRCOR: An air corridor (AIRCOR) is a restricted air route of travel for friendly aircraft. Its function is to prevent friendly forces from firing on friendly aircraft. Its altitudes are not more than the coordinating altitude, when there is one.
x-enum-descriptions.AIRRTE: An air route (AIRRTE) is the navigable airspace between two points, with only the identification that is necessary to apply flight rules. It is a bi-directional route. It can go through air defences as a minimum-risk route. Only support traffic uses it.
x-enum-descriptions.APPCOR: An approach corridor (APPCOR) is airspace for the safe passage of land-based aircraft that join a maritime force or go from it. The corridor usually goes from an entry and exit gate to the centre of the force. Its inner boundary is the identification safety range (ISR).
x-enum-descriptions.LLTR: A low-level transit route (LLTR) is a temporary low-level corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area. It decreases the risk to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces.
x-enum-descriptions.MRR: A minimum-risk route (MRR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions that the ground commander recommends for aircraft. It has the minimum known hazards to low-flying aircraft that transit the combat zone. Aircraft usually use it to cross the forward line of own troops (FLOT). It is usually not near close air support (CAS) target areas.
x-enum-descriptions.SAAFR: A slow aviation assets flight route (SAAFR) is a route below the coordination level for land component aviation assets in the forward area. The route is for their movement in direct support of ground operations.
x-enum-descriptions.SC: A special corridor (SC) is an air corridor for the special routing requirements of some missions in air operations.
x-enum-descriptions.SL: A safe lane (SL) is a bi-directional lane from an airbase, a landing site or a base defence zone (BDZ) to adjacent routes or corridors. It can connect more than one of them. Safe lanes can also connect adjacent activated routes or corridors.
x-enum-descriptions.TC: A transit corridor (TC) is a bi-directional corridor in the rear area that routes aircraft through friendly air defences with minimum risk. Air traffic services are not normally available in it.
x-enum-descriptions.TMRR: A temporary minimum-risk route (TMRR) is a temporary minimum-risk route for air traffic. It goes between transit routes, or the rear boundary of the forward area, and its operations area. The route is for direct support of ground operations.
x-enum-descriptions.TR: A transit route (TR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area for air operations. It decreases the risks to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces. It is a bi-directional route, and it should avoid weapons free zones and base defence zones.
x-enum-descriptions.VFRRTE: A published visual flight rules route (VFRRTE) is a route on a chart for visual flight rules (VFR) flights around, under or through complex airspace, such as class B airspace. A VFR flyway is a general flight path, not a specific course, and it needs no air traffic control (ATC) clearance. A VFR corridor goes through class B airspace with defined vertical and lateral limits, and it needs no ATC clearance. A VFR transition route is a specific flight course on a chart. On it, communication with ATC is necessary, and an ATC clearance is necessary in class B airspace.

vertices.description: This list contains the names and points of the vertices of the route, in order. A vertex that is not in the list has no name.

items.description: A route vertex is a vertex of the route geometry with its name or its point record.

index.description: This field gives the position of the vertex in the route geometry, from 0 at the start. The vertices of a path are the start of each segment and the end of the last segment. The index shall be smaller than the number of vertices, and the indexes shall increase in the list.

name.description: This field gives the name of this route vertex, for display. An example is the charted name of a visual reporting point.

point.description: This field identifies the point record that is at this vertex.

measure-route.title: Air route or corridor

measure-tl.description: A traverse level (TL) is the vertical displacement above low-level air defence at which aircraft can cross the area. It is a height and an altitude. It gives the defenders one more procedure to identify friendly aircraft. The record gives the level as a height above the ground and as an altitude above mean sea level.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this traverse level is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this traverse level has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this traverse level and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the vertical geometry of the traverse level: a height above the ground and an altitude above mean sea level.

id.description: This field identifies this traverse level. Other records and orders use it to refer to this traverse level.

name.description: This field gives the name of this traverse level, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this traverse level, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this traverse level. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a traverse level. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

measure-tl.title: Traverse level

measure-volume.description: An airspace coordination volume is an airspace with a name and given dimensions, made of components in sequence. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling. The type is a code from North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) AJP-3.3.5 Annex B or from doctrine. The code gives the task of the volume and the airspace users that can or cannot go in it. The agency that controls the volume does the coordination of entry and operations.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this airspace coordination volume is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

channels.description: This list identifies the communications channels of this airspace coordination volume.

components.description: This list contains the airspace components of the volume, in order. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling.

controlling_agency.description: This field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace coordination volume.

coordination_instructions.description: This list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace coordination volume has an effect on.

description.description: This field gives the information about this airspace coordination volume and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this airspace coordination volume. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace coordination volume.

name.description: This field gives the name of this airspace coordination volume, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this airspace coordination volume, as free text.

purpose.description: This field gives the task or objective of this airspace coordination volume, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace coordination volume. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

restrictions.description: This list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace coordination volume.

type.description: This field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.

x-enum-descriptions.AARA: An air-to-air refuelling area (AARA) is airspace of defined dimensions for air-to-air refuelling operations. Other airspace users stay out of it, unless they coordinate with its controlling authority.
x-enum-descriptions.ACAR: An airspace control area (ACAR) is airspace with lateral limits that follow the boundaries of the area of operations. It is the basic geographic element of airspace control. It can contain airspace control sub-areas.
x-enum-descriptions.ACCA: An airborne command and control area (ACCA) is airspace of defined dimensions, only for aircraft that do battlefield command and control.
x-enum-descriptions.ADIZ: An air defence identification zone (ADIZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the identification, location and control of aircraft is immediately necessary.
x-enum-descriptions.ADS: An air defence sector (ADS) is a geographical subdivision of an air defence region. An air defence region is a geographical subdivision of an air defence area.
x-enum-descriptions.AEWA: An airborne early warning area (AEWA) is airspace of defined dimensions, only for aircraft that do airborne early warning.
x-enum-descriptions.ALTRV: An altitude reservation (ALTRV) is a block of altitude for aircraft to transit or loiter. The altitude reservation is moving or stationary. It always has an upper and a lower limit, and it can also have lateral limits.
x-enum-descriptions.BDZ: A base defence zone (BDZ) is airspace around a base that increases the effectiveness of its air defence systems. Transit routes should avoid it.
x-enum-descriptions.BZ: A buffer zone (BZ) is airspace that is a buffer between coordination measures. It is an air reference measure, thus aircraft go through it without coordination.
x-enum-descriptions.CADA: A coordinated air defence area (CADA) is a block of airspace that a land-based air commander and a naval commander agree together. They agree it when their forces operate close to each other. It sets the limits of their air defence responsibilities.
x-enum-descriptions.CBA: A cross-border area (CBA) is a temporary segregated area above an international boundary for a specified operational need. Only its designated users can fly in it.
x-enum-descriptions.CCZONE: A carrier control zone (CCZONE) is an area around an aircraft carrier that operates fixed-wing or rotary-wing aircraft. The carrier controls the area for carrier flight operations.
x-enum-descriptions.COZ: A crossover zone (COZ) is airspace beyond the missile engagement zone (MEZ) of a maritime force. Air defence fighters may go into it only in hot pursuit of targets, to complete an interception. The fighters give a countdown of the seconds until the engagement.
x-enum-descriptions.DZ: A drop zone (DZ) is a specified surface area onto which aircraft airdrop airborne troops, equipment or supplies. Aircraft and fires should deconflict with the drop operations.
x-enum-descriptions.EC: An electromagnetic combat (EC) is airspace only for aircraft that do missions of electromagnetic combat, which is electronic warfare.
x-enum-descriptions.FACA: A force air coordination area (FACA) is an area around a force in maritime operations, in which airspace control and air defence measures are necessary. The measures prevent mutual interference between all friendly surface and air units and their weapon systems.
x-enum-descriptions.FEZ: A fighter engagement zone (FEZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the engagement of air threats is normally the task of fighter aircraft. This definition is for air defence.
x-enum-descriptions.HIDACZ: A high-density airspace control zone (HIDACZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates. In it, many different weapons and airspace users operate in a concentrated volume. Aircraft coordinate their entry with its controlling authority.
x-enum-descriptions.JEZ: A joint engagement zone (JEZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in air defence, in which more than one air defence system engages air threats. These systems are surface-to-air missiles (SAMs) and aircraft, and they engage at the same time. The `OPTASK AAW` sets its limits. Accurate identification and positive control are necessary, thus SAMs do not engage friendly fighters.
x-enum-descriptions.LZ: A landing zone (LZ) is a zone that aircraft use for landing.
x-enum-descriptions.NFZ: A no-fly zone (NFZ) is a zone of airspace of defined dimensions for specified functions. In it, no aircraft may operate, unless the enforcing authority authorizes the operation.
x-enum-descriptions.PZ: A pickup zone (PZ) is an aerial retrieval area, in which aircraft pick up personnel or materiel.
x-enum-descriptions.RCA: A reduced coordination (RCA) is airspace of defined dimensions in which general air traffic may fly off-route. General air traffic controllers do not have to start coordination with operational air traffic controllers for these flights.
x-enum-descriptions.RECCE: A reconnaissance area (RECCE) is airspace only for aircraft that do reconnaissance.
x-enum-descriptions.ROZ: A restricted operating zone (ROZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates for a given situation or operational need. Examples are refuelling orbits, holding, fires and landing or drop zones. It restricts the operation of one or more airspace users in it.
x-enum-descriptions.SAFES: A safety sector (SAFES) is a sector that routes friendly aircraft to maritime forces with minimum risk. In it, friendly aircraft are safe from friendly fighters or weapons when they approach or return to the maritime force.
