action.description: This field gives the task of this step, as free text.

completion.description: This field gives the condition at which this step is completed, as free text.

condition.description: This field gives the condition in which this step is applicable, as free text.

resources.ReportDefinition.description: A report definition is a report that a unit should send. ATP 6-02.x and the standard operating procedure (SOP) of the unit give the report.

channel.description: This field identifies the radio channel that is for the report.

classification.description: This field gives the highest security classification of the data in the report, as one of the enumerated values.

format_ref.description: This field gives the reference to the format of the report, as free text. Examples are a paragraph of a standard operating procedure (SOP) and a USMTF format.

frequency.description: This field gives the interval at which units send the report, such as `Daily NLT 0600` or `On event`, as free text.

medium.description: This field gives the transmission method of the report, as one of the enumerated values.

name.description: This field gives the name of this report, for display. Examples are `SITREP`, `LOGSTAT` and `CASREP`.

precedence.description: This field gives the message precedence of the report, as JP 6-0 gives it, as one of the enumerated values.

recipient.description: This field identifies the command and control agency that receives the report.

submitter.description: This field gives the unit or staff section that has the task to send the report, as free text.

trigger.description: This field gives the event or schedule that causes a unit to send the report, as free text.

agencies.description: This map contains the command and control agencies. The key of each item is its identifier.

aircraft_types.description: This map contains the aircraft types. The key of each item is its identifier.

areas.description: This map contains the planning areas that are not control measures. The key of each item is its identifier.

channels.description: This map contains the radio channels. The key of each item is its identifier.

comm_plans.description: This map contains the communication plans, which are named sets of radio assignments that flights share. The key of each item is its identifier.

control_measures.description: This map contains the control measures. The key of each item is its identifier.

emitters.description: This map contains the emitters, which are air defence radars with their systems and threat rings. The key of each item is its identifier.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

facs.description: This map contains the forward air controllers. The key of each item is its identifier. A controller contact of an air tasking order (ATO) can identify a forward air controller of this map. An identifier shall not be in `agencies` and in `facs`.

instrument_procedures.description: This map contains the instrument procedures that airfields refer to. The key of each item is its identifier.

localizers.description: This map contains the localizers to which airfields and the ends of runways refer. The key of each item is its identifier.

notams.description: This map contains the notice to air missionses (NOTAMs) that planners write before the operation. The key of each item is its identifier.

pattern_profiles.description: This map contains the traffic pattern profiles that airfields refer to. The key of each item is its identifier. A traffic pattern profile in this map shall not refer to a traffic pattern profile.

places.description: This map contains the operating locations for departure, recovery, diversion and transport: airfields, carriers and forward arming and refuelling points (FARPs). The key of each item is its identifier.

procedures.description: This map contains the procedures. The key of each item is its identifier.

reports.description: This map contains the report definitions that taskings refer to in their report requirements. The key of each item is its identifier.

routes.description: This map contains the routes. The key of each item is its identifier.

scls.description: This map contains the standard conventional loads (SCLs). The key of each item is its identifier.

stores.description: This map contains the weapons, pods, tanks and other stores. The key of each item is its identifier.

targets.description: This map contains the fixed targets, mobile targets and area targets. The key of each item is its identifier.

threats.description: This map contains the possible threats. The key of each item is its identifier.

contingencies.description: This list contains the instructions for contingencies on the route.

name.description: This field gives the name of this route, for display.

points.description: This list contains the points of the route, in order. The points are in the sequence of the flight.

action.description: This field gives the flight phase at this route point, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.approach: At this point, the flight starts its approach to an airfield for the landing.
x-enum-descriptions.departure: The flight starts its route from the departure airfield at this point.
x-enum-descriptions.egress: This value identifies the egress from the task area.
x-enum-descriptions.hold: The flight holds at the point.
x-enum-descriptions.ingress: This value identifies the ingress to the task area.
x-enum-descriptions.recovery: At this point, the flight starts to go back to an airfield after the task.
x-enum-descriptions.transit: This value identifies a transit between two points.

altitude.description: This field gives the altitude that the order gives for this route point, as an altitude with its unit and reference.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this route point. Other records and orders use it to refer to this route point.

instructions.description: This list contains the instructions for this route point.

name.description: This field gives the name of this route point, for display.

number.description: This field gives the steerpoint number of this route point in the aircraft, from 1.

position.description: This field gives the geographic position of the route point, as latitude and longitude.

speed.description: This field gives the speed that the plan gives for this route point, as a speed with its unit.

timing.description: This field gives the time condition for the flight at this point. The condition is at a time, in a window, not before a time, not after a time, or on order.

resources.Speed.description: A speed is a speed with its unit: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour.

unit.description: This field gives the unit of the speed: knots, kilometres in one hour or Mach number, as one of the enumerated values. The suffix `_ias` identifies an indicated airspeed (IAS), and the suffix `_tas` identifies a true airspeed (TAS).

value.description: This field gives the value of the speed, in the unit of `unit`.

resources.Speed.title: Speed

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

family.description: This field gives the store family, such as `AIM-120` for an `AIM-120C`, as free text. A load variant can use a different store of the same store family.

kind.description: This field gives the type of store, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.cargo: This value identifies a load in the aircraft that goes to other units.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a store that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.pod: This value identifies a pod with sensors or other equipment, such as a targeting pod. The aircraft does not release it.
x-enum-descriptions.rack: This value identifies a store that has other stores on it.
x-enum-descriptions.tank: This value identifies an external fuel tank.
x-enum-descriptions.weapon: This value identifies a weapon, such as a missile, that the aircraft fires or drops.

name.description: This field gives the name of this store, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this store, as free text.

role.description: This field gives the function of the pod, as one of the enumerated values. Only a store of the `pod` type shall have a role.

x-enum-descriptions.datalink: This value identifies a pod that sends data to the weapons of the aircraft or receives data from them.
x-enum-descriptions.emitter_targeting: This value identifies a pod that finds enemy radars and gives their positions to weapons such as the high-speed anti-radiation missile (HARM).
x-enum-descriptions.navigation: This value identifies a pod with sensors for navigation at night or at low altitude.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a pod with a function that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.reconnaissance: This value identifies a pod that collects images or other data for reconnaissance.
x-enum-descriptions.self_protection_jamming: This value identifies a jammer that gives protection to the aircraft that has it.
x-enum-descriptions.tactical_jamming: This value identifies a jammer that attacks enemy radars and radios for other aircraft.
x-enum-descriptions.targeting: This value identifies a pod that finds, tracks and designates targets.

airfield.description: This field identifies the operating location that is the base of the threat, for example the airfield of enemy aircraft.

area.description: This field identifies the planning area or control measure in which the threat operates.

as_of.description: This field gives the time of the threat data.

briefing.description: This list contains the attachments for the brief on this threat. An attachment is an image, a map, a document or a link.

description.description: This field gives the data about this threat and its local conditions, as free text.

emitters.description: This list identifies the emitters that are a part of this threat.

expected_activity.description: This field gives the possible operations of the threat, as free text.

kind.description: This field gives the type of threat, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.air_defense: This value identifies surface-to-air weapons, such as surface-to-air missiles (SAMs) and air defence guns.
x-enum-descriptions.electromagnetic: This value identifies an electromagnetic threat to radio or radar equipment.
x-enum-descriptions.environmental: This value identifies a dangerous condition from the weather or the terrain.
x-enum-descriptions.other: This value identifies a threat that the other values do not include.
x-enum-descriptions.surface: This value identifies surface forces other than air defence.

name.description: This field gives the name of this threat, for display.

source.description: This field identifies the source document. The reference identifies the document. It may also give a revision and a locator.

system.description: This field gives the system of the threat, such as `2K12 Kub`, as free text.

resources.Window.description: A window is a time interval with limits that are absolute date-times or offsets from the period of the order that contains it.

runway.description: A runway is one runway with its two ends, its dimensions and its surface. Each end has the threshold, the heading and the equipment that is necessary for a flight simulator.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

airfield.description: This field identifies the airfield that has this runway. In the runway list of an airfield, the value shall be the identifier of that airfield.

designator.description: This field gives the designator of the runway, for example `03L/21R`. The value shall contain the designators of the two runway ends, with `/` between them.

ends.description: This list contains the two ends of the runway. The two ends shall have opposite designators. Each runway end in the airfield has a different designator.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

id.description: This field identifies this runway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this runway.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a runway record. The value selects this navigation contract.

length.description: This field gives the published length of the runway, as a length with its unit.

name.description: This field gives the name of this runway, for display.

provenance.description: This field gives the provenance of this runway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this runway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

source.description: This field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example `FAA CIFP cycle 2610`. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field `provenance` gives the same facts as structured data.

surface.description: This field gives the surface of the runway, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.hard: This value identifies a surface of asphalt, concrete or an equivalent hard material.
x-enum-descriptions.soft: This value identifies a surface of gravel, grass or ground, without asphalt or concrete.
x-enum-descriptions.water: This value identifies an area of water that seaplanes use as a runway.

width.description: This field gives the published width of the runway, as a length with its unit.

runway.title: Runway

runway.ArrestingGear.description: An arresting gear is one cable or barrier across the runway that stops aircraft.

distance_from_threshold.description: This field gives the distance from the landing threshold of this end to the cable, as a length with its unit.

type.description: This field gives the type of the arresting gear, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.BAK_12: This value identifies the `BAK-12` arresting gear with a cable.
x-enum-descriptions.BAK_13: This value identifies the `BAK-13` arresting gear with a cable.
x-enum-descriptions.BAK_14: This value identifies the `BAK-14` arresting gear with a cable that retracts.
x-enum-descriptions.BAK_15: This value identifies the `BAK-15` barrier with a net.
x-enum-descriptions.E_28: This value identifies the `E-28` arresting gear with a cable.
x-enum-descriptions.E_5: This value identifies the `E-5` arresting gear with a chain.
x-enum-descriptions.MA_1A: This value identifies the `MA-1A` barrier with a net and a cable.

runway.Lighting.description: Runway lighting is the approach lights, the runway lights and the visual slope indicator.

approach_lighting.description: This field gives the approach lighting system, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.ALSF_1: This value identifies `ALSF-1`: a high intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights, for Category `I` approaches.
x-enum-descriptions.ALSF_2: This value identifies `ALSF-2`: a high intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights, for Category `II` and `III` approaches.
x-enum-descriptions.MALS: This value identifies `MALS`: a medium intensity approach lighting system.
x-enum-descriptions.MALSF: This value identifies `MALSF`: a medium intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights.
x-enum-descriptions.MALSR: This value identifies `MALSR`: a medium intensity approach lighting system with runway alignment indicator lights.
x-enum-descriptions.ODALS: This value identifies `ODALS`: an omnidirectional approach lighting system.
x-enum-descriptions.SSALF: This value identifies `SSALF`: a simplified short approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights.
x-enum-descriptions.SSALR: This value identifies `SSALR`: a simplified short approach lighting system with runway alignment indicator lights.
x-enum-descriptions.SSALS: This value identifies `SSALS`: a simplified short approach lighting system.

edge_lights.description: The value is `true` when the runway has edge lights. The value is `false` when the runway has no edge lights.

reil.description: The value is `true` when the runway end has runway end identifier lights (REIL). The value is `false` when the runway end has no REIL.

slope_indicator.description: This field gives the visual slope indicator for the approach, as one of the enumerated values.

x-enum-descriptions.PAPI: This value identifies the precision approach path indicator (PAPI). It is one row of light units that show the aircraft position in relation to the approach path.
x-enum-descriptions.VASI: This value identifies the visual approach slope indicator (VASI). It is two or three rows of light units that show the aircraft position in relation to the approach path.

runway.RunwayEnd.description: A runway end is one end of a runway and the landing direction to that end. It has the threshold, the heading, the approach equipment and the local pattern values.

arresting_gear.description: This list contains the arresting gear across the runway. Distances are from the threshold of this end.

designator.description: This field gives the designator of this runway end. It is the magnetic heading in degrees divided by 10, with an optional suffix `L`, `R`, `C`, `W`, `S`, `G` or `U`.

displaced_threshold.description: This field gives the distance from the runway end to the displaced threshold, as a length with its unit. The record does not have this field when the landing threshold is at the runway end.

heading.description: This field gives the bearing of the runway in this landing direction, as a bearing with its unit and reference. A magnetic heading includes the declination of the airfield. Thus, a consumer can calculate the true heading from it.

lighting.description: This field gives the runway lighting for this landing direction.

localizer.description: This field identifies the localizer that is for this runway end. The field `runway` of the localizer shall identify this runway end.

threshold.description: This field gives the geographic position of the landing threshold for this landing direction, as latitude and longitude.

threshold_crossing_height.description: This field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the approach path, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the approach path above the landing threshold.

threshold_elevation.description: This field gives the elevation of the landing threshold above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.

traffic_pattern.description: This field gives the traffic pattern values for this landing direction. They replace the values of the airfield pattern, and each value is optional.

scl.description: A standard conventional load (SCL) is one store configuration of one aircraft type. It gives the stores of each aircraft, their stations and fuzes, the gun rounds and the countermeasures. The load does not show that it is possible to install the stores on the aircraft.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

aircraft_type.description: This field identifies the aircraft type that this load is for. Each flight with this standard conventional load (SCL) shall have this aircraft type.

code.description: This field gives the standard conventional load (SCL) code of the load, such as `4G12.3A.1X.2`. Some units use these short codes. They are not a standard for all units. OpenAIX does not use the code to find the stores. The stores and the stations of the record are the reference.

countermeasures.description: This field gives the chaff, the flares and the countermeasure program of the load.

era.description: This field gives the era of the load, such as `modern` or `retro`, as free text. The unit sets its eras.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

gun_rounds.description: This field gives the number of gun rounds in each aircraft.

id.description: This field identifies this standard conventional load (SCL). Other records and orders use it to refer to this SCL.

kind.description: The value identifies this record as a standard conventional load (SCL).

laser_code.description: This field gives the default laser code for the weapons of this load. A store entry can give a different code.

missions.description: This list contains the tasking families and roles that this load is applicable to. The list shall include the tasking of each flight that has this load as its primary load.

name.description: This field gives the name of this standard conventional load (SCL), for display. An example is `AI-1 GBU-12`.

remarks.description: This field gives the remarks about the load, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.

scl_number.description: This field gives the number of the load in the table of the unit, such as `DTA05` or `101`, as free text.

source.description: This field identifies the source document. The reference identifies the document. It may also give a revision and a locator.

stations.description: This list contains the weapon stations of the load, with the stores on each station.

stores.description: This list contains the stores of the load, with the quantity of each store in each aircraft. This list does not give the stations. Each store shall occur one time in the list. With stations, the quantity of each store shall be equal to the sum on its stations.

variant_tags.description: This list contains the labels of this load variant, such as `120B` or `Pre-2015`. Each label shows a difference from the other load variants with the same number.

scl.title: Standard conventional load

scl.Countermeasures.description: A countermeasure load is the chaff, the flares and the dispenser program of a load.

chaff.description: This field gives the number of chaff cartridges in each aircraft.

flares.description: This field gives the number of flares in each aircraft.

program.description: This field gives the countermeasure program of the dispensers, as free text.

scl.Fuze.description: A fuze setting is the fuzes of a weapon, their function and their time adjustments. The `extensions.sim.dcs` data of a station keeps the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) values of the fuze.

arming_delay_s.description: This field gives the time after the aircraft releases the weapon until the fuze can operate, in seconds.

delay_ms.description: This field gives the time after the weapon hits the target until the fuze functions, in milliseconds.

function.description: This field gives the function of the fuze, as one of the enumerated values.

height_of_burst.description: This field gives the height above the ground at which the fuze functions, as a length with its unit.

nose_fuze.description: This field gives the nose fuze of the weapon, such as `DSU-33`, as free text.

tail_fuze.description: This field gives the tail fuze of the weapon, such as `FMU-139`, as free text.

scl.SCLMission.description: A standard conventional load (SCL) mission is a tasking family and a role for which the load is applicable.

role.description: This field gives the role or mission type in the tasking family, as one of the enumerated values. It agrees with the `role` field or the `mission_type` field of the tasking. If the entry does not give a role, the load is applicable to all roles of the tasking family. The role shall be a role of the tasking family.

tasking.description: This field gives the tasking family, as the `kind` field of an air tasking order (ATO) tasking gives it, as one of the enumerated values.

scl.StationLoad.description: A station load is the stores on one weapon station of the aircraft.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

items.description: This list contains the stores on this station.

rack.description: This field identifies the store of the `rack` type that has the other stores on this station.

station.description: This field gives the label of the weapon station in the flight manual or the simulator, such as `3` or `5L`, as free text. Each station shall occur one time in the list of stations.

scl.StoreLoad.description: A store load is one store of a load with its quantity, fuze, laser code and program.

fuze.description: This field gives the fuze setting of the store.

laser_code.description: This field gives the laser code of the store. It replaces the laser code of the standard conventional load (SCL) for this store.

program.description: This field gives the weapon program of the store, as free text.

quantity.description: This field gives the number of items of the store in each aircraft, or on the station in a station entry.

store.description: This field identifies the store that this entry is for.

territory.description: A territory is a land area with an affiliation: friendly, hostile or neutral. The required shape gives the boundary, and it has priority over the country codes. Thus a territory can be in a real, a historic or a fictional world. Without vertical limits, a territory runs from the surface with no upper limit.

$schema.description: This field identifies the schema that validates this document.

active.description: This field gives the time interval during which this territory is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.

affiliation.description: This field gives the affiliation of the territory, as one of the enumerated values. The values are the standard identities friend, hostile and neutral of `MIL-STD-2525` and `APP-6`.

x-enum-descriptions.friend: This value identifies land that friendly forces hold or that is friendly to them.
x-enum-descriptions.hostile: This value identifies land that enemy forces hold or that is hostile.
x-enum-descriptions.neutral: This value identifies land that is neither friendly nor hostile, for example a neutral country.

countries.description: This list contains the country codes of the territory, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes such as `SYR`. The codes are labels for maps of the real world. The geometry gives the boundary.

description.description: This field gives the information about this territory and its local conditions, as free text.

extensions.description: This field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group `sim` contains the simulator data of the record.

geometry.description: This field gives the horizontal geometry of the territory: a polygon or a GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon (RFC 7946).

id.description: This field identifies this territory. Other records and orders use it to refer to this territory.

lower_limit.description: This field gives the floor of the territory: an altitude with its reference, or the surface. This field is optional; without it, the floor is the surface.

name.description: This field gives the name of this territory, for display.

notes.description: This field gives the notes about this territory, as free text.

resources_ref.description: This field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this territory. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.

type.description: The value identifies this record as a territory. The value is the same for all territories.

upper_limit.description: This field gives the ceiling of the territory: an altitude with its reference, or no limit. This field is optional; without it, the territory has no upper limit.

territory.title: Territory
